Unreachable today because no test module uses an expected failure. Filed now rather than when somebody writes the first one, because at that point the number will look right and be wrong.

title: the header-rule net cannot see a walk that loses one real reader file, and could not before TASK-244 either
to: The header-rule net can see a walk that loses a whole reader DIRECTORY and cannot see one that loses a single reader FILE — and could not before the round that widened it either, so this is the remaining half of an older hole rather than damage from that round. Per-file loss was never expressible in the corpus, whose entries are per-directory.

title: TASK-244's docstring and result say eight whole-tree scans where the instrumented count is twelve
to: A round's docstring and its result document both say eight whole-tree scans where the instrumented count is twelve. The delta is right and the cost claim rests on the delta, which is why it was not charged. The four unaccounted scans are one test scanning inside a loop, so the number counts call SITES where the runtime counts CALLS — and that is the same slip the round already fixed once in a neighbouring docstring while leaving this one standing.

title: a markdown code fence disables the dispatch.md paragraph while its presence guard stays green
to: A markdown code fence disables the paragraph a procedure depends on while the guard checking that paragraph is present stays green. The reviewer filed rather than failed, and the reason is the interesting part: an HTML comment renders as nothing, so a guard staying green over one asserts a reader sees text no reader can see — but fenced prose still renders and is still read. Whoever takes this should decide whether the guard is about BYTES PRESENT or about A READER SEEING, because those two readings diverge here for the first time.

title: scan_spec_escalations' docstring still carries the premise its own round refuted, and now contradicts perry-lint's
to: A parser's docstring still carries the premise its own round measured false, and now contradicts the corrected copy in perry-lint. The round deliberately left the parser alone, because touching it would have broken the byte-identity carrying an earlier parity result forward without re-earning it — the right call for that round, and it leaves the two docstrings disagreeing with the parser's being the wrong one. Cheap to fix now that the parity no longer needs protecting.

title: git_ancestor can be made to never report anything stale and all 24 provenance tests stay green
to: A green mutation, filed rather than charged: map one function's error return to True — so nothing is ever reported stale — and all 24 provenance tests still pass. The reason is exact: the test pins only the True and None answers and never the False case, which is the only answer staleness reporting depends on. The shape is worth more than the instance — a three-valued function whose tests pin two values leaves the third free, and here the free one is the whole point of the feature.

title: TASK-304's result page closes with a false sentence about a lint rule that is deliberate and already recorded
to: A result document closes with a false sentence about a lint rule that is deliberate and already recorded. The reviewer checked the round's own alarm and found it half right: the non-monotonicity is real and was reproduced at its source, but it is documented, and the payload DOES record which ids came back clean — so the round's closing claim that nothing records it is false here. Correct the page and open no further row.

title: tests/parallel:371 names the wrong file as the guard for its own audit wiring
to: A comment names the wrong file as the guard for its own audit wiring: the file it points at is byte-identical to base and contains no occurrence of the term at all. The guard is real and lives elsewhere, so this is a pointer defect rather than a missing guard. Worth a row because a comment that sends a reader to the wrong file to verify a claim costs the next reader exactly the time the comment was meant to save.

title: a design back-reference lives in a cell the close path clears, so a finished design reports as never handed off
to: THE FILED TITLE IS NOW MISLEADING AND THE ROW IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. Its 'a cell the close path clears' half was already fixed two days before the row was even filed. The deliverable was never that half: it asks for a task to carry its design id in a field the lifecycle does not destroy, counted structurally. Re-measured 2026-09-03 and the state is WORSE than at filing — the design now reports eleven implementation references, all of them incidental prose mentions, while its six real implementation rows contribute zero. The signal flipped from a false positive, which was visible, to a false negative, which is not.

title: the register updated field carries two facts, so appending an edge silently re-dates every asserted number in the file
to: ONE WORD OF THE TITLE IS FALSE: not 'silently' — the writer already warns on every write that would re-date an asserted KR, naming each one. The defect is disclosed at three layers and fixed at none. The real and unfixed half is that one `updated:` field carries two different facts, 'when the register changed' and 'when the KR numbers were asserted', written at one site and read as freshness at another. The consequence is that staleness is computable only register-wide, so a report of 'stale 0' is not evidence that any individual number is fresh. The cheapest wrong outcome here is a fourth disclosure.

title: TASK-067's bound claims names resolve through `NAME = "…"` bindings, and that is false for its own f-string clause
to: A bound claims that names resolve through simple assignment bindings, and that is false for its own f-string clause. NOT URGENT, and that is measured: none of the six shapes exists in the tree today, so the bound is correct about the current tree and wrong only about what it promises for a future one. The risk is the next round trusting the prose. Two citation slips in the same file are to be fixed in the same pass.

title: dispatch.md tells an agent to branch but never to isolate, so a subagent switches the SHARED working tree and the PMO's writes land on its branch
to: dispatch.md tells a dispatched agent to branch but never to isolate, so a subagent switches the SHARED working tree and the PMO's own writes land on that agent's branch. Blocked awaiting a user decision after the round exhausted its review budget with two failures.

title: test_project_root_resolution reddens under the parallel runner while agent worktrees are live — TASK-258's disease in a second module
from: FOUND 2026-09-03 while landing TASK-182, and NOT ATTRIBUTED YET -- the correlation is strong and the mechanism is unproven, which is the difference this row has to close. Measured: 3 of 23 tests in test_project_root_resolution fail under tests/parallel -j 4; all 23 pass under python3 -m unittest on the same tree, same moment; three agents were concurrently writing worktrees at .claude/worktrees/, which are NESTED INSIDE this repository and each carry a full .perry/ and perry/. The module's subject is resolving a project root by walking, so a walk that reaches a nested worktree finds another project root -- but I did not prove that is what happens. TASK-258 fixed exactly this disease in tests/test_tree_guard.py (its own title: 'copies the LIVE repository, so any concurrent write reddens it') and is done, so the precedent and probably the technique already exist in that file's fixture.
to: REPRODUCED TWICE MORE 2026-09-03, after the TASK-182 and TASK-283 merges: 3 of 23 red under tests/parallel -j 4, 23/23 green under python3 -m unittest on the same tree seconds later, with 34 nested agent worktrees present under .claude/worktrees/. So the correlation now has three observations and the mechanism still has zero -- that gap is the row. TASK-258 fixed the same disease in tests/test_tree_guard.py and is done, so the technique probably already exists in that file's fixture. DO NOT ACCEPT THE CORRELATION AS THE CAUSE: the verification requires removing the worktrees (or pointing the walk away from them), showing the parallel run goes green, restoring them, and showing it goes red again. A control that does not flip both ways has not identified anything.

title: TASK-285 has FAILed two V4 rounds and perry-lint says another round is not the next step. UNUSUALLY, THE PRINCIPLE HAS ALREADY BEEN NAMED -- by the round 2 reviewer, not by me -- and I have already implemented it. This ask exists to have you confirm or overrule that, because a PMO who has just fixed something is the worst judge of whether the principle is settled. WHAT HAPPENED. The row writes one rule into three shipped files: a dispatched agent works in its own git worktree, the primary checkout is never switched by an agent and merges the branch afterwards. Round 1 defeated the guard by softening the rule to 'MAY ... where convenient' -- every assertion pinned the presence of words, none pinned modality. I fixed that with a denylist of eight hedge words. Round 2 then kept the pinned imperative VERBATIM, used none of the eight, and added one sentence inside the rule's own blockquote: 'Where a worktree is impractical, sharing the primary checkout instead is an acceptable alternative.' All nine tests reported OK with the headline deliverable retracted. It also walked past the push check with two synonyms (publishes / raises a pull request). Its summary: A DENYLIST OVER ENGLISH HAS NOW LOST THIS ARGUMENT TWICE. THE OPTIONS. (a) IMPLEMENTED AND MY RECOMMENDATION -- an allowlist. The rule block is compared literally and four normative regions are pinned by sha256; any addition, removal or rewording reddens. Rationale prose is deliberately NOT pinned, so the observed-failure account and the local-merge argument can still be improved without touching a test; what an agent is TOLD TO DO cannot change silently. Thirteen mutations, thirteen red, including both that defeated the old design and a single extra space. Cost: changing the rule now requires re-pinning a digest in the same commit, which is friction on purpose. This is the same move you chose in USER-904 (one header_index over a smarter detector) and USER-906 (one invariant over a fourth predicate). (b) Keep a denylist and widen it again. The record says this is the third widening and the first two each looked principled. (c) Accept the guard as advisory, close at a lower rung, document the limit. (d) Drop the guard entirely and rely on the fact that the rule is now in three files a reader sees. STATED LIMIT OF (a), because it is real: an allowlist pins what EXISTS and cannot cover a fifth normative region someone adds later in a file it does not read. Evidence: evidence/2026-09/TASK-285-round2-v4-review.md and TASK-285-result.md.
answer: 决定 2026-09-03（用户拍板，Perry 推荐 a）：选 (a) —— 白名单。规则块逐字比对，四个规范性区域按 sha256 钉死；任何增删改写都变红，包括没人预料到的那种。理由散文故意不钉：观察记录和本地 merge 的论证可以继续改进而不动测试，不能悄悄变的是 agent 被要求做什么。代价接受：以后改这条规则必须在同一个提交里重新钉一次摘要，这个摩擦是有意的。不选 (b) 再拓宽黑名单 —— 那已经输了两次，第三次也只是猜下一个没被列进去的词。已实现，13 个突变 13 红。声明的限制保留在记录里：白名单只能钉住已存在的规范性文字，日后有人在它读不到的文件里新加第五处，它看不见。

title: TASK-067 has FAILed two V4 rounds and needs a principle chosen, not a third round. THE CENSUS THAT MAKES THIS ANSWERABLE NOW EXISTS: TASK-323 delivered a bound and a census and PASSED V4 round 2 on 2026-09-03, so unlike the last two rounds this choice is against measured numbers rather than a recollection. Both failed rounds carried criteria-unbounded because the criteria file had no bound; it now has one -- 89 members (27 W1 / 18 W2 / 38 R1 / 6 R2), last element viewer/tables.py:280, generated by a runnable script at evidence/2026-09/TASK-323-bound.py. Census: 20 rows, 12 caught, 8 uncaught, plus 13 shape rows with 4 red controls. THE TWO READINGS, with what each would actually have to cover. (A) EVERY WRITE PATH MUST REFUSE AN UNRENDERABLE CELL. Population is all writers. To close it must cover all 27 W1 members, already refusing, PLUS the 7 uncaught separator-row builders -- perry-task:985, :1034, :1112, :5174, perry_md_store.py:774, perry-goals:327-328, perry-goals:3093 -- PLUS bin/perry-decide:332, which guards with a weaker third spelling that misses a trailing newline, PLUS perry-task:7431. It would NOT cover the five uncaught read shapes, which are not writes. Its cost is visible in the bound itself: the population has no last element other than the current line count, which is exactly why this file had no bound for two rounds and why each round found a member the previous one never reached. (B) ONE CHOKE POINT PLUS ONE DETECTOR, MY RECOMMENDATION. To close it must cover ONE SYMBOL -- nothing outside render_row builds a row -- with ragged-row as the backstop. The census says precisely what that buys and what it does not: it covers the 7 separator builders by construction IF separator rows are routed through the choke point too, which they are not today; its backstop is MEASURED to work on w4-w7 and MEASURED not to exist for r2/r3/r4/r7/r8; ragged-row cannot cover the read side at all and .split('|', 6) proves no count-based check ever will; its detector has four demonstrated blind spots on the read half because SPLIT_RE matches none of maxsplit, re.split, a SEP constant, or .rsplit/.partition; and it does not reach perry-decide:332, which builds no rows. TWO MORE FACTS THE ROUNDS DID NOT HAVE. First, ragged-row fires ONLY inside a table the schema recognises -- round 1 confirmed with a control that the identical 8-cell row is silent in an unrecognised section -- so on a project filing work under its own headings via add --group, which Perry explicitly supports, (B)'s backstop does not exist. Second, both readings leave perry-task:7431 open; it is a message-quality defect rather than a corruption path. PRECEDENT, OFFERED AS PRECEDENT AND NOT AS AN ARGUMENT: you chose shape (B) in USER-904 after seven rounds and USER-906 after three. The census neither confirms nor contradicts that -- (B)'s one-symbol surface is real and measured, and so is the fact that its detector is green on nine shapes, five of which have no backstop of any kind. Evidence: evidence/2026-08/TASK-067-finding.md sections Bound, Census and The two readings; evidence/2026-09/TASK-323-round2-v4-review.md.
answer: 决定 2026-09-03（用户拍板，Perry 推荐乙/B）：选 (B) —— 一个收口点。除 render_row 外没有东西构造表格行，守卫变成一个符号的检查面。这是本项目第三次选这个形状（USER-904 的 header_index、USER-906 的 shrink 不变量）。THE THIRD OPTION WAS OFFERED AND NOT TAKEN: 我另外提过「(B) 收口 + 把甲那 9 处里真正会写坏数据的 8 处也做掉」，用户选的是 (B) 本身，所以那 8 处不在这次范围内。因此实现时必须明确以下三点，它们是 (B) 买到的和没买到的，普查已经量过：(1) 7 个分隔行构造点只有在分隔行也被路由进收口点时才被覆盖 —— 今天没有，所以路由分隔行是 (B) 的一部分而不是附加项；(2) bin/perry-decide:332 不构造行，(B) 够不着它，它仍然开着；(3) bin/perry-task:7431 两种读法都不覆盖，是消息质量缺陷不是损坏路径。最重要的一条，按 Perry 的推荐记录：不要把 ragged-row 当成 (B) 的卖点。普查测出它在 w4-w7 有效、在 r2/r3/r4/r7/r8 不存在，读取侧有四个已证实盲点（maxsplit、re.split、SEP 常量、.rsplit/.partition），而且只在 schema 认得的表格里触发 —— round 1 用对照确认，同样的 8 格行放在不被识别的 section 里报 0 错误，所以用 add --group 的项目上这张网根本不存在。这些洞要写成声明的限制，不能让下一轮以为有兜底。

title: dispatch.md tells an agent to branch but never to isolate, so a subagent switches the SHARED working tree and the PMO's writes land on its branch
reason: USER-914 answered (a); the principle is settled, so a further round is no longer forbidden

title: The writer can destroy the table it writes to, and perry-lint cannot see it
from: SCOPE HAS DECAYED -- re-derive it before starting; do not work from the cell this replaces. That cell justified the row with four live hazards and at least two are now false, measured 2026-09-02 on d49964e. (1) "perry-decide still writes DECISIONS.md" is FALSE: DECISIONS.md appears 7 times in bin/perry-decide and every one is a comment or docstring, no write site -- TASK-235 removed the index and its deliverable holds. (2) "perry-migrate still rewrites a stranger's files" is FALSE: bin/perry-migrate was deleted 2026-08-31 by TASK-261. (3) "perry-goals still writes OKR.md section Commitments in place" appears to still hold -- perry-goals commit is documented as that write path -- but confirm it rather than inherit it. (4) "ragged-row is still the only catch" is DOUBTFUL: TASK-203 landed foreign-table-shape refusals across risks, intake and asks with store preservation and renamed key columns (evidence/2026-08/TASK-203-round5-v4-review.md), so the catch is no longer alone. The row's underlying question -- can a writer still destroy the table it writes to without perry-lint seeing it? -- may still be a real P0, but its population must be re-measured before anyone estimates the work. It is also still blocked on TASK-095, which has been in review 3.8 days and is the same stall holding TASK-099.
to: UNBLOCKED 2026-09-03 by USER-915: reading (B) chosen -- one choke point, nothing outside render_row builds a row. STILL NEEDS A SPEC; the choice is made, the work is not. THREE THINGS THE SPEC MUST CARRY, all measured by TASK-323's census and none of them optional. (1) Routing the 7 separator-row builders through the choke point IS PART OF (B), not an extra: perry-task:985/:1034/:1112/:5174, perry_md_store.py:774, perry-goals:327-328, perry-goals:3093. (B) covers them by construction only if they are routed, and today they are not. (2) bin/perry-decide:332 builds no rows, so (B) does not reach it -- it stays open and needs its own row. (3) bin/perry-task:7431 is covered by neither reading; message quality, not corruption. AND THE RECOMMENDATION THE USER'S ANSWER CARRIES: do NOT sell ragged-row as (B)'s backstop. Measured present for w4-w7, measured absent for r2/r3/r4/r7/r8; four demonstrated read-side blind spots (maxsplit, re.split, a SEP constant, .rsplit/.partition); and it fires ONLY inside a schema-recognised table -- confirmed with a control, the same 8-cell row is silent in an unrecognised section, so on a project using add --group the net does not exist. Those holes are declared limits in the deliverable, not caveats to discover later. The third option -- (B) plus fixing the 8 corruption sites from reading (A) -- was offered and NOT taken.

title: The writer can destroy the table it writes to, and perry-lint cannot see it
Split perry-task by subcommand group
to: bin/perry-task is to be split into one file per subcommand group. The split is deliberately left unsized for now: the markdown reader, the row renderer and the cell escaping are all on their way out of that file, and re-measuring once they are gone is cheaper than splitting it twice.

title: Agent is five strings that do not join, and role has never once been written
to: Perry represents an agent as five separate strings that never join into one record, and the `role` field has never once been written on any row. Who owns the agent register was settled on 2026-08-20 — work owns `.perry/agents.jsonl` and `.perry/roles/` — so what the row still needs is a spec before it can be dispatched.

title: four of six document collections are unreachable through any contract
to: Four of Perry's six document collections cannot be reached through any published contract. Deferred on 2026-08-21 by the user, with the cost recorded rather than waved through: aiMark reads those directories directly for now, which knowingly makes it a second reader of Perry's LAYOUT, so a consumer holding `perry/design/` breaks silently the first time a project moves its state root.

title: ## Cadence becomes a store
to: Perry keeps six registers as JSONL stores that tools read and write through. `BOARD.md § Cadence` is not one of them and is still a markdown table nothing owns. This row converts it.

title: Perry has no writer for a migration event, so TASK-180 hand-wrote JSON into an append-only log
to: Perry records every other kind of event through a writer that owns the event's shape. A migration event has no writer at all, so TASK-180 appended hand-written JSON straight into the append-only event log.

title: a write returns no seq, so a poll cannot tell a stale read from a fresh one
to: A Perry write returns no sequence number. So a consumer that polls has no way to tell whether what it just read already reflects its own write or predates it, and a stale read is indistinguishable from a fresh one.

title: no compare-and-set on a write, and the board demonstrably moves between a read and a write
to: Nothing lets a caller say 'write this only if the board is still what I read'. There is no compare-and-set on a Perry write, and the board demonstrably does move between a read and the write that follows it, so two writers can silently overwrite each other.

title: perry-diagnose asks 'is this ask answered' with a word search over free prose, and disagrees with the store in both directions
to: perry-diagnose answers 'has this ask been answered?' by searching for words in free prose rather than by reading the ask register. It disagrees with the store in both directions — reporting answered asks as pending and pending ones as answered.

title: an Objective is not a record, so it has no durable address
to: An Objective has no id, so nothing can point at one durably: `okr.objectives[].id` is empty for all five. The phase level already solved exactly this — `phase/002-linkage.md` states `id: O1` and the payload carries it — and the contract already accepts a STATED id where it refuses a derived one. DESIGN-009 was drafted for it on 2026-08-21 with four user decisions still open.

title: OKR setting is a ten-field checklist where it should be an elicitation
to: Setting an OKR is currently a ten-field checklist to be filled in, where it should be an elicitation that draws the answers out. DESIGN-011 was drafted for it on 2026-08-21 with four user decisions open. Its step 2 is the real gate: run the question bank against a project that has no OKR.md and score the output with the rubric, or the claim that the rubric surfaces zero issues is not measured at all.

title: DESIGN-006 F — a finance-shaped role runs one real task end to end
to: The first role card for work that is not software — a finance-shaped role, run end to end on one real task. All four dependencies are done, so it is startable; the real blocker is that every role card shipped so far is software-shaped, so this is the first honest test of whether the role model generalises. The run itself and its V5 signature stay with the user.

title: writing about an id costs a dangling entry, and three records tonight paid it
to: Writing about a task id in prose costs a dangling-reference entry, and three records did on one night. The row is to decide the rule for the five dangling ids that resulted — widen the report's mark beyond the paragraph, exempt evidence records wholesale, or accept the cost in writing — and then make the reconcile test assert whichever was chosen.

title: Nothing tells an agent a projection is behind its store — ADR-012's rule has no surface
to: ADR-012 decided that an agent should detect when a projection is behind the store it is derived from, and nothing in Perry surfaces that. This is the whole implementation of the detection half: a per-pair mtime comparison replacing about 3,100 lines of drift census. Perry's own history is the argument for building the surface rather than writing the instruction — an instruction with nothing behind it does not get run.

title: the tasks store is the only one of six whose census line does not name it: 'store: 225 record(s)' and 'drift against the store', where the other five say risks/OKR/config/intake/ask store
to: Perry reports six stores and names five of them. The tasks store alone prints `store: 225 record(s)` and `drift against the store`, where the other five say risks store, OKR store, config store, intake store and ask store — so the one line a reader is most likely to be looking at is the one that does not say what it is about.

title: viewer/parsers.py:3899-3900 builds top_risks from BOARD.md while perry/risks.jsonl exists, reached from perry-state:1631 — the task and OKR readers beside it already prefer their stores (TASK-095 V4 round 1, finding 4)
to: The top-risks reader still builds its answer from `BOARD.md` even though `perry/risks.jsonl` exists and is canonical. The task and OKR readers sitting next to it in the same file already prefer their stores, so this one reader is the odd one out rather than the norm.

title: test_risks_store's TestTheReadersAreOneFunction fails 3 assertIs identity checks under 'unittest discover' and passes under 'bash tests/run' and in isolation — a module-double-import artifact, independently observed by two reviewers on 2026-08-29; the suite's answer depends on the runner and nothing says so
to: A test module passes when run alone and fails three identity assertions when run under `unittest discover`, because of a module double-import artifact. Two reviewers observed it independently on 2026-08-29. The defect worth fixing is not the assertions: it is that the suite's answer depends on which runner invoked it and nothing anywhere says so.

title: perry-config write --from-file writes a zero-record store at exit 0 on a config.md with no settings, and every perry-task/perry-goals write is then refused forever while verify/diff/lint all report zero drift — the same command is both the cause and the only offered recovery (TASK-095 round 3, finding 2)
to: One command can put a project into a state only that same command is offered to repair, and it cannot. Run against a config file carrying no settings, `perry-config write --from-file` writes a zero-record store and exits 0; every subsequent task and goals write is then refused forever, while verify, diff and lint all report zero drift and so report nothing wrong.

title: tracks_source is on two published payloads (perry-state project.config, perry-diagnose work_modes) with four possible values and no entry in schema/ or reference/ — raised by two consecutive TASK-095 reviewers
to: `tracks_source` appears on two published payloads with four possible values and has no entry in the schema or in any reference page — so a consumer reading it has to guess what the values mean. Two consecutive reviewers raised it before it was filed.

title: test_host_support.TestOpenCodeDispatchLimit.test_concurrent_mixed_registers_do_not_exceed_global_cap is FLAKY under the parallel runner — red once on 2026-08-29 with an empty ~/.cache/perry/in-flight, green in isolation and green on two consecutive tests/run re-runs; same class as the already-filed queue-reconcile and scratchpad-baseline parallel races
to: A host-support test is flaky under the parallel runner: red once on 2026-08-29 with an empty in-flight cache, green in isolation and green on two consecutive re-runs. Same class as the queue-reconcile and scratchpad-baseline races already on the board — a concurrency defect that only appears under load.

title: duplicate ids: a duplicate on the BOARD silently deletes a stored risks/asks record on an ordinary write (risk_records/ask_records skip a seen id), and a duplicate IN THE STORE leaks one record's cleared onto the other and re-persists it — both predate TASK-203 and were unreachable before it
to: Duplicate ids destroy records silently, in two different directions. A duplicate on the BOARD deletes a stored risks or asks record on an ordinary write, because the record builders skip an id they have already seen; a duplicate IN THE STORE leaks one record's cleared state onto the other and then persists it. Both predate TASK-203 and neither was reachable before it.

title: a hand-REORDERED .perry/config.md § Tracks table is config-store-drift to perry-lint and silent to every other tool — defensible under principle A as written, but neither documented nor guarded; found by the TASK-095 round 6 V4 reviewer, who also notes records_out_of_stored_order and cells_wearing_decoration were each verified against only one fixture
to: Re-ordering the tracks table in `.perry/config.md` by hand reads as config-store drift to perry-lint and as nothing at all to every other tool. The behaviour is defensible under the principle as written, but it is neither documented nor guarded. The reviewer who found it also notes that two neighbouring behaviours were each verified against only one fixture.

title: after intake-sweep leaves the canonical intake store empty, perry-lint reports perry/intake.jsonl as NS-01 foreign state even though the intake contract says an empty file is still a store; recognize Perry's declared empty intake store without excusing a foreign same-name JSONL
to: After an intake sweep empties the canonical intake store, perry-lint reports `perry/intake.jsonl` as foreign state Perry did not write — even though the intake contract says an empty file is still a store. The fix has to recognise Perry's own declared empty store without also excusing a foreign file that happens to share the name.

title: Thin perry-state to a query over the six JSONL stores; the payload shape does not change
to: perry-state exists because `BOARD.md` was canonical and counting anything meant parsing a markdown table. With six JSONL stores the counting is a loop, so what is left worth keeping is the payload SHAPE it publishes, not its reader. DESIGN-014's user decision 1 was answered on 2026-09-01: thin it to a query over the stores rather than keeping or deleting it, and the published shape does not change.

title: The render must distinguish what is projected from what is canonical — TASK-199's scope on the surface ADR-010 creates
to: A render has to show which of the things it prints are canonical records and which are projections of them, or a reader cannot tell what is safe to edit. Blocked in practice on the two rows that create the render this property has to hold on. It replaces TASK-199, which carried the same scope and was dropped in error on 2026-09-01 in a way that could not be reversed.

title: DESIGN-015 F — P003-O3-KR2 is computed from the store and events, not asserted
to: The sixth row of DESIGN-015. It is what turns phase KR P003-O3-KR2 from a number somebody typed into a number something counted, by computing it from the linkage store and the event log. It should not be allowed to lag the rest of the sequence for that reason.

title: DESIGN-015 E — phase/<NNN>-linkage.md sheds its schema'd half
to: The fifth row of DESIGN-015: `phase/<NNN>-linkage.md` sheds the half of itself that is schema'd data once that data lives in the store. Separable and allowed to lag — unlike the add-time writer it does not gate P003-O3-KR2 — and it is DESIGN-013 hygiene rather than work serving that KR.

title: DESIGN-015 A — declare linkage.jsonl in claims[] and write its three record schemas
to: The first row of DESIGN-015's implementation plan, locked 2026-09-02: declare `linkage.jsonl` in Perry's claims list and write the three record schemas it will hold. Section 7 of that design carries the risk this creates — a new claimed path means a new namespace-collision warning in every existing Perry project.

title: DESIGN-015 B — import the 93 linkage records from phase/003-linkage.md into the store
to: The second row of DESIGN-015: import the linkage records that currently live in `phase/003-linkage.md` into the new store. The count filed with the row is a measurement rather than an estimate, so it is to be re-measured before importing and the difference reported if the register has moved.

title: DESIGN-015 C — move the six linkage readers to the store
to: The third row of DESIGN-015, and the one the whole sequence turns on: move the six linkage readers onto the store. It MUST land before the add-time writer, and the ordering is a hard constraint rather than a preference — a writer pointing at a store the readers have not moved to fails silently, with the edge landing while every reader still answers from the old document.

title: DESIGN-015 D — add --kr writes the edge, and the add event carries kr
to: The fourth row of DESIGN-015: `perry-task add --kr` writes the linkage edge itself and the add event carries it, which is what moves phase KR P003-O3-KR2 off zero. Blocked on the reader migration by the hard ordering constraint that row records. The design flags its own reading of user decision 3 as an interpretation, so if an explicit never-asked record was intended, this row changes with it.

title: a locked decision that gets no task row does not ship, and nothing links a design's plan step to the work that discharges it
to: Two directions of one missing edge, and this row is the design-to-task half: a locked design's plan step has no link to the work that discharges it, so a decision that gets no task row simply does not ship and nothing notices. Its sibling covers the task-to-design direction. Whoever picks either up should first decide whether one declared edge answers both, because two mechanisms for one relationship is how this project acquires a second translation table.

title: a locked design's implementation rows need not cite it, so a finished design reports as never handed off forever
to: The task-to-design half: an implementation row need not cite the design it implements, so a finished design can report as never handed off forever. The trap was measured as it fired — filing this row took DESIGN-001 from `impl_refs` 0 to 1 and emptied the pending list, with nothing implemented, because the counter is a literal text match. So the defect is two-sided: six real implementation rows count for nothing, and one row that merely says 'read DESIGN-001' counts as implementing it.

title: Measure the category split inside perry-task and perry-lint by call site, not by grep
to: Measure how bin/perry-task and bin/perry-lint split by CATEGORY, counted at the call site rather than by grep. It is the first step of DESIGN-014's implementation plan and the precondition for that document's central section being a measurement rather than an admission: the two files are 40% of bin/ and neither of them is one thing.

title: Sweep bin/, viewer/ and tests/ for document handling that ADR-007 made dead
to: Sweep bin/, viewer/ and tests/ for document-handling code that ADR-007 made dead, and report what is dead against what is still load-bearing. Round 1 is the CENSUS only: the fence this row is eventually for is blocked on a product decision, and the phase says outright that the measurement is the input the user needs in order to answer it. The round does not fence anything and does not close the row.

title: the Bound that review.md requires is never asked for where specs are written, so its absence costs rounds instead of minutes
to: review.md requires a bounded criterion and perry-lint reports its absence, but add-task — the only place a spec is ever written — never mentions `## Bound`. So specs are authored without one and the omission surfaces rounds later, which is a measured cost rather than a style preference: one row burned five review rounds, another eleven, and a census found the unbounded finding eight times across twelve review files.

title: nothing warns against writing a cross-reference to a row that has not been minted yet, and the id it guesses may land on the row doing the guessing
to: Nothing warns an author against writing a cross-reference to a task id that has not been minted yet, and the id guessed may land on the row doing the guessing. Observed when a row's next action said 'unlike TASK-280' predicting what the NEXT row would be numbered, and that row was itself minted as TASK-280, making the sentence self-referential. The existing rule forbids an example id that resolves to nothing; this one resolves, to the wrong row.

title: git-boundaries.md never says how to write a commit message, and Perry's own identifiers are backticked, so a -m string silently executes them
to: The git-boundaries page never says how to write a commit message, and Perry's documentation convention is backticked identifiers — so a `-m` string containing them has them executed by the shell and substituted away. It happened: a commit explaining the escalation gate's false positives named two fragments and shipped with both names simply gone. This bites Perry harder than most projects because nearly every honest commit message about its own code contains backticks.

title: perry-task's --actor is optional and defaults, so a write to a lane-owned file can have no owner any session can claim
to: perry-task's `--actor` is optional and defaults, so a write to a lane-owned file can end up with no owner any session can claim. The actionable core is that optional actor, NOT the incident that exposed it — five link edges were written that the session filing this could not account for, and the edges themselves turned out to be correct. The tool's own help already states the open question: DESIGN-004 asks whether actor should be mandatory and until that is answered an unset actor is recorded as unset.

title: the dispatch gate matches a path a spec CITES as if the spec wrote it, so an honest spec is refused and an incidental mention green-lights a real hit
to: The dispatch safety gate matches a path a spec merely CITES as though the spec were going to write it. Both directions are live and one is silent: honest specs are refused for naming the evidence file the round exists to produce, and one spec passed only because an incidental mention elsewhere cancelled a real hit, with no output distinguishing that from a genuinely clean scan. Same defect family as a design-id counter that cannot tell 'implements' from 'mentions' — a literal matcher standing in for intent.

title: close-task warns after the fact on a V4 whose verdict block cannot be parsed, so 10 of 27 V4 closures carry a rung nothing confirms
to: close-task lets a V4 closure through when its verdict block cannot be parsed, and perry-lint reports it only afterwards — so a rung can be claimed and merely questioned later, which is not a gate. Scoped to the FORWARD half: refuse the close. Whether the ten existing closures in that state should be re-reviewed or restated rewrites this project's own verification record and belongs to the user.

title: goals has no KR writer, so adding a KR means hand-editing okr.jsonl — build the writer
to: There is no write path for a KR record at all, so adding, restating or withdrawing one means hand-editing a file the documentation says is never edited by hand. It is now blocking a decided pivot: the user decided to withdraw a phase KR, the pivot procedure offers exactly that operation, and the tooling cannot perform it. The deliverable should cover both levels — the overall KRs in okr.jsonl and the phase KRs in the linkage file.

title: every NS-01 warning Perry emits is about a file Perry itself wrote, and the remedy each one offers is a no-op
to: Every namespace-collision warning Perry emits is about a file Perry itself wrote, and the remedy each one offers is a no-op — the warnings say 'move Perry's state to its own root' and the state root already IS that root. One of the five is a separate bug: a FILE claim whose warning tells the reader to move files out of a file. This is why every lint run reported warnings that every session skipped as pre-existing; a check that only ever cries wolf gets trained out of the reader.

title: the objective scanner's heading-depth test does not cover the claim its own docstring makes
to: A scanner's heading-depth test does not cover the claim its own docstring makes. Reported by a reviewer as a green mutation and correctly not charged as a failure — a green mutation is a finding either way, and here it is the second half of one: the guard does not test what it says it tests.

title: a store record's title field is unverifiable: planted garbage passes verify with drift 0 and byte_identical true
to: A store record's title field is unverifiable: plant garbage in it and `verify` still reports drift 0 and `byte_identical: true`. It matters because that sentence is what every store row in this project rests its acceptance on, and it is silent about any field the renderer does not read. Found while attacking a load-bearing claim and correctly ruled pre-existing rather than that row's defect.

title: a dispatched agent's pkill matches across the whole machine and killed another agent's suite
to: A dispatched agent's process cleanup matches across the whole machine and killed another agent's test suite. This is what concurrency looks like when the isolation is per-worktree but the process table is shared: the dispatch limit reserves slots and nothing scopes a signal. Worth pairing with the finding that the shared scratchpad is not private either — both are the same shape.

title: DESIGN-014's per-tool line counts drifted and were not re-measured at lock
to: DESIGN-014's per-tool line counts drifted and were not re-measured when the document was locked. Small on its own, but that document's whole method IS per-tool measurement, so a stale figure in it is the document failing its own standard rather than a typo.

title: bin/perry-config --help names perry-conform, a tool TASK-261 deleted
to: bin/perry-config's help text names a tool that was deleted. The argument that decides it came from the consumer who reported it: the guidance says to believe the contract table over the help text, but the help text is what a person actually runs — so Perry told a consumer to prefer one surface over another instead of fixing the one people invoke.

title: schema/README.md still tells a consumer to read the State root out of .perry/config.md, which is the render
to: schema/README.md tells a consumer to read the state root out of `.perry/config.md`, which is the projection rather than the register. Measured 2026-09-02, and the measurement makes the fix sharper than 'the page is stale': the tool resolves the state root itself and publishes it, including on a project that has no store, so a consumer that can run the tool never needs to parse the markdown and one that reads the store alone would get it wrong.

title: an evidence document produced a line count with an instrument that walks the filesystem, so it counted untracked bytecode
to: A line count in an evidence document was produced by an instrument that walks the filesystem rather than the git index, so untracked bytecode was counted into it. The lesson this row should carry is about instruments and about propagation: the wrong REASON for the wrong number had already been written into a locked design document, and correcting the board cell did not correct the artifact. A reviewer found it there and failed the round, correctly. A finding already written down somewhere needs the write chased, not just the record amended.

title: DESIGN-014's D-02 entry cites the branch by a moving ref, so its figure stops re-deriving the moment the branch advances
to: A design document's entry cites the branch it measured by a moving ref, so its figure stops re-deriving the moment that branch advances. Recorded by two consecutive reviewers and deliberately not charged by either, because it sits outside the round's bound and the review rules forbid widening one except by filing a row. This is that row. The item had already degraded further between the two rounds, which is the argument for it rather than against it.

title: green_lit does not de-duplicate across touches sections while refuse does
to: One half of a spec-scanning function de-duplicates across sections and the other half does not. Deferred in 2026-08 with a stated condition — the next change to that function — and the condition has now fired, so the deferral discharges into a row rather than expiring silently, which is the whole point of attaching a condition to one. Still cosmetic today: no spec repeats a fragment across two sections.

title: parsers.py:462 says the walk is skipped when handed an exact root, and the code walks four levels anyway
to: A parser's docstring says the walk is skipped when it is handed an exact root, and the code walks four levels anyway. CLOSING IT COSTS MORE THAN THE DOCSTRING GAP SUGGESTS and a correct fix will look like a regression unless it lands with its tripwire: the minimal fix turns another round's deliberate anti-vacuity test red, so whoever takes this must retire or invert that test in the same commit. Whether the minimal form is green suite-wide is unverified and should be established first.

title: three more fixtures carry a .perry/ with no events.jsonl, so the four-parent walk leaves them too
to: Three more test fixtures carry a `.perry/` directory with no event log, so the same parent walk escapes them too. Inert today for exactly one reason — none of the three ships a design directory — and adding a single design document to any of them re-opens the defect there with no warning and no test. Sequence it after the walk fix: if that makes the walk honour an explicit root, these three may need nothing at all.

title: 127 of 134 specs carry no ## Bound, and the check that would say so can only fire after the round it would have bounded
to: Almost every spec on this project — 127 of 134 — carries no `## Bound`, and the check that would report that cannot fire until after the round it would have bounded. The check is implemented and correct and it reports two, because it reads the criteria field OF A VERDICT BLOCK — so a spec is only reachable once a review has already been written against it. A post-hoc check on a pre-flight property. The two it does fire on belong to the row that failed two review rounds and hit the schema limit: it found the unboundedness by paying for it twice.

title: a dispatched agent's entire round lives in its context until one final commit, so any interruption costs all of it
to: Nothing a dispatched agent does reaches disk until its single terminal commit, so an interruption at any point before that costs the whole round. Measured on 2026-09-02: five agents were dispatched, the laptop was closed, all five died at the watchdog and git log across all five branches shows zero commits. Between fifteen and thirty minutes of work each, and the only surviving trace was the last sentence each had streamed. The cause was environmental, which is exactly why the row exists — an agent cannot prevent the interruption, but it can refuse to hold a round hostage to a single terminal commit.

title: two comments in tests/test_tree_guard.py assert evidence the round could not have measured and a set it did not enumerate
to: Two comments in a test file assert evidence the round could not have measured and a set it did not enumerate. One claims zero differences where 843 of 846 file modes differ; the other calls a file 'the only other file the copied run executes' where the enumeration finds twenty-four. Both are documentation defects against a round that passed on everything behavioural, and one edit closes both.

title: test_host_support.py admits four registrations through a gate whose global cap is three, and the runner calls it a flake without naming the mechanism
to: A host-support test admits four registrations through a gate whose global cap is three, and the runner's own docstring calls the module a known flake without naming the mechanism — which is the problem, because a named flake with an unnamed mechanism is indistinguishable from a real concurrency defect, and this one reads like one. Attributed rather than waved away: the module is red on a pristine archive of the base commit, one run in four under load.

title: test_tree_guard.py is now the suite's longest module at 48-124s, and its own fix is what put it there
to: This test module is now the suite's longest at 48-124 seconds, and its own fix is what put it there. It is NOT a regression and should not be read as one — the round that did it just passed review, and both of the things that cost the time are load-bearing. So the question is not whether the cost is justified but whether it is the right size. The 48-124 second spread is itself the first finding: the module's cost varies 2.6x with machine load.

title: the dispatch limiter has a race, found while three rounds ran concurrently
to: Perry's limiter for concurrent dispatches has a race in it, found while three review rounds were running at once. Reported by a round that deliberately left it outside its own bound, and filed here so the refusal discharges into a row rather than into a sentence in a result document. The limiter is the only thing coordinating concurrent agents on this machine, and five ran at once the night it was found.

title: a test-id fixture hard-codes the 3.11 id shape while its docstring says it was copied from a real run, and python3 here is 3.9.6
to: A test fixture hard-codes the test-id shape produced by Python 3.11 while its docstring claims it was copied line for line from a real run — and the interpreter this project actually runs is 3.9.6, where the ids collapse to the class name. Counts are unaffected, which is why it was not charged. The part worth knowing beyond this fixture is that two interpreters are in play here and they disagree about test identity.

title: a module red only from an unexpected success reports zero failed tests, the exact shape the fix argues against
to: A module made red only by an unexpected success reports zero failed tests — the exact zero-failures-under-a-red-module shape the fix that shipped argues against, arriving through the one door its guard does not cover. Unreachable today because no test module uses an expected failure. Filed now rather than when somebody writes the first one, because at that point the number will look right and be wrong.

title: the header-rule net cannot see a walk that loses one real reader file, and could not before TASK-244 either

The agent still needs that list, but it can read the document directly. Decide whether that half goes too and say why either way -- do not delete it silently and do not keep it silently. The written procedure is the deliverable, the deletion is the easy half. THE CORPUS THE PROCEDURE MUST HANDLE, measured 2026-09-03 across all 148 specs: 133 pass, 15 refuse, 0 unarmed. Five refusals are citation false positives the procedure must let through -- TASK-099 ('setup and hook code that reads repository documents -- read.'), TASK-108 (matches the tool names bin/perry-diagnose and tests/test_diagnose.py), TASK-139 ('changing it is escalated. If the design points that way, stop and file'), TASK-220 (cites adopt/diagnose as a router precedent), TASK-244 (the English noun in 'the harness re-does setup per test', which its own spec header already hand-annotates). One is a true refusal the procedure must still catch: TASK-107, on ~/.claude/skills, the ln -s variants, publish, rm -rf and --force-with-lease. ONE THING THE SCANNER KNEW THAT THE PROCEDURE MUST NOT LOSE: path_root_is_foreign recognises a foreign root BY the characters ~ $ < {, which is why TASK-290's round-1 agent REFUSED an instruction to narrow the character class -- narrowing it would have made ~/other-project/evidence/2026-09/ re-root and stop refusing. Whatever that function knew has to be said in words in the procedure.
to: THE REPLACEMENT PROCEDURE'S CORE, salvaged from TASK-290's V4 reviewer when the row was superseded mid-review. It had read viewer/parsers.py:4446 first-hand and restated path_root_is_foreign in words, which is exactly what dispatch.md must now carry: RELATIVE IS INTERNAL, full stop -- a relative path resolves against the scanned project's root and cannot name anyone else's tree. FOREIGN IS FIVE SHAPES: absolute (/srv/...), home (~/...), variable ($PERRY_HOME/...), upward (../...), and an UNRESOLVED ROOT (<target>/..., {{project}}/...). That last clause is a deliberate safe-direction judgement -- a root nobody has resolved is not a root known to be this project -- and the reviewer flagged it as the clause a prose rewrite is most likely to drop, because it is the only one not obvious from an example. THE TRAP THE PROCEDURE INHERITS, and this is the sharpest thing on this row: the characters that IDENTIFY a foreign root are the same characters you would strip as formatting noise. _PATH_CHAR admits ~ $ < > { } * precisely BECAUSE those mark a foreign root; narrowing it re-roots ~/other-project/evidence/2026-09/ into project/evidence/2026, which then reads as this project's own tree and stops refusing. A prose rule has the identical collision -- 'ignore the markdown around the path' and '~ means someone else's home' are the same character. THEREFORE THE PROCEDURE MUST STATE OWNERSHIP DETECTION BEFORE ANY NORMALISATION STEP. TWO RECORDED GATE-DIRECTION DEFECTS pointing OPPOSITE ways, from the round's own documents and unreproduced by the reviewer: bold or a sentence-final full stop cleared a declared claim-surface write (refuses too little), while bolding an own-tree path **perry/evidence/...** makes it refuse (refuses too much, because the head reads as **perry and * means foreign). Formatting alone moved the verdict in both directions -- the strongest single piece of evidence for why this scanner is being removed rather than fixed. ONE NUMBER TO SETTLE BEFORE RELYING ON IT: my census says 148 specs scanned, 133 pass, 15 refuse; round 2's own result says 147 scanned, 16 refused. The reviewer verified neither and flagged the disagreement. Re-derive it in this row rather than inheriting either figure.

Three guards locate a function with next() and never check it is the only one
summary: Each of the three source-reading guards does next(n for n in ast.walk(...) if it is a FunctionDef named X). Python binds the LAST top-level definition of a name; ast.walk yields the FIRST. So a duplicate definition placed earlier in the file becomes the guard's target while the real one is what runs, and the guard reports on code nobody executes.

title: Three guards locate a function with next() and never check it is the only one
to: FOUND BY TASK-332's ROUND-2 V4 AND PASSED AS A FINDING RATHER THAN A FAILURE, on reasoning I agree with: the hole needs DEAD CODE NO AUTHOR WRITES -- a duplicate top-level def -- whereas round 1 of TASK-332 broke on INNOCENT edits, which is a different severity; the next(...) formulation is verbatim what TASK-332's own round-1 reviewer prescribed as the fix; and it is a three-site project pattern, one of which is TASK-331's guard that the same reviewer had passed 5 of 5. So the pattern was blessed twice before anyone tested it. THE MECHANISM, exactly: Python binds the LAST top-level definition of a name, ast.walk yields the FIRST. Plant a duplicate 'def summary_shape' earlier in the module carrying both rule literals and a padded register, then delete the real register in full -- ALL 3,253 TESTS GREEN. The round's claim that 'no edit anywhere else in the module can move the target' is therefore false. THE THREE SITES, which I confirmed: tests/test_row_integrity.py:616, tests/test_summary_is_asked_for.py:286 and :347. TWO ONE-LINE FIXES THE REVIEWER VERIFIED: assertEqual(len(fns), 1) after collecting all matches, or read lib.summary_shape.__doc__ off the imported object and drop ast entirely -- the second removes the class of defect rather than guarding against it, and is worth arguing for. WHAT NOT TO BREAK: the nested, conditional, decorator and async attacks all FAIL to defeat these guards today, because ast.walk is breadth-first so a real depth-1 definition always wins. A fix that changes that behaviour has traded one hole for another. ONE MORE THING THE REVIEWER MEASURED: the emptiness floor on the register overclaims -- replacing the whole register with a token line plus 720 characters of the letter x passes it. The floor establishes that the register is LONG, not that it is prose, and the docstring should say so.

title: The suite has no unit seam: 324 subprocess launches stand in for calling a function
to: MEASURED BY THE PMO 2026-09-04, ALL STRUCTURAL -- no timing figure here was taken on this machine while it was loaded, and one that was is explicitly discarded below. THE SHAPE: 3,265 test methods; 324 subprocess call sites across 101 of 124 modules; per tests/durations.json 103 modules with a recorded duration summing to 1,853s serial, median module 9.7s, only 11 modules under 1s, 34 over 20s, and the slowest twelve are 44% of the total (test_track_move 95.0s, test_goals_writer 86.2s, test_purge 86.0s, test_diagnose 83.2s, test_rung_vocabulary 72.7s). WHAT THE TESTS NAME: the call counts point at COMMAND-LINE TOOLS rather than functions -- perry-task 83, perry-state 76, perry-lint 67, perry-goals 35, perry-tasks 28, perry-explain 19, perry-diagnose 19, perry-decide 9. THE COST PER CALL: each subprocess.run starts a fresh interpreter that parses bin/perry-task's 7,851 lines and imports viewer/parsers.py's 4,627 plus perry_store.py, all before reaching the one judgement under test. That is pure overhead and it is paid 324 times. A FIGURE I TRIED TO TAKE AND AM DISCARDING: I measured a bare 'python3 -c pass' at 4,467ms and 'perry-task --help' at 15,324ms while load average was 114 on 14 cores. Both are meaningless. Whoever takes this row must measure on an idle machine and say so. SUBPROCESS COUNT IS NOT THE WHOLE STORY: the slowest module, test_track_move at 95s, has only FOUR subprocess calls and 30 tests -- it builds a fixture project per test, mkdir .perry, write config.md, write BOARD.md, then spawn a CLI to seed the store. So the row must account for fixture construction as well as process launch. THE DIAGNOSIS, and it is the point of the row: THIS PROJECT HAS ALMOST NO UNIT SEAM. Logic lives in executable scripts rather than importable modules, so the only way to reach a judgement is to run the whole program as a black box. THE EVIDENCE IT IS FIXABLE: TASK-263's census measured bin/perry-task at 61% TYPED -- most of the logic is already deterministic functions, merely locked inside an executable. And bin/lib/__init__.py is the working counter-example: summary_shape is imported and called directly, and those modules are among the fastest. THE OTHER PAYOFF: today's whole flake family is a consequence of using the filesystem and the process scheduler as a test fixture -- TASK-334 a file vanishing mid-walk, TASK-341 a probe written into the live tree, TASK-357 a concurrent timing assertion, TASK-335 a control that decays with the clock, TASK-356 a sentinel colliding with prose. A test that imports a function and calls it has none of those failure modes. WHAT THIS ROW MUST NOT BECOME: a deletion of tests. The suite has already been cut and sped up several times and the shape did not change, which is the reason this row exists. The converted module must keep every assertion it has, and the before and after counts must be quoted and equal.

perry-restore-check --root cannot verify a git-archive scratch copy — the exact use review-constraints.md recommends
summary: Every V4 round is told to do destructive mutation work in a scratch copy and then verify the restore with perry-restore-check --root <copy>. That call cannot work: --root repoints the tool's git queries as well as its file paths, so against a git archive copy, which has no git history, it answers '<ref> is not a commit in <copy>'. The procedure Perry hands every reviewer is broken at the step that matters most, and reviewers have been silently falling back to hand-rolled byte comparison instead.

title: Two concurrently dispatched agents share one 'session-specific, isolated' scratchpad and can overwrite each other's files mid-round
summary: Agents dispatched into separate git worktrees are isolated in the tree but not on disk: they are handed the same session scratchpad path. On 2026-09-07 two V4 reviewers ran concurrently and one overwrote the other's mutation harness while it was in use. The affected round noticed, re-verified its copies against the ref and renamed its harness, so nothing false was reported -- but it noticed by luck, and a round that did not notice would report mutation results produced by another agent's file.

title: One malformed line in linkage.jsonl voids validation of every good record in the file

All five rows at review -- TASK-278, TASK-336, TASK-341, TASK-356, TASK-357 -- have ZERO verdict documents naming them, and all five have their code MERGED ON MAIN. Method, with its control: grep -rl "^task: <ID>$" perry/evidence/ returns the verdict blocks naming a row; run against TASK-276 and TASK-277, whose rounds landed today, it returns exactly their two review documents, so the detector works. 41 distinct tasks carry a verdict block in the whole repository; none of the five is among them. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DEFECT: perry-lint --reviews reports v4-close-without-verdict 11 times, verdict-malformed 12 times and review-rounds-exhausted once -- it guards the EXIT, a row closed at V4 without a verdict, and says NOTHING about a row PARKED at review without one. Parking is exactly where the 2026-09-04 rate limit left everything: it killed the reviewers mid-round, their branches carry stubs, and nothing re-dispatched them or noticed. TASK-276 sat that way from 09-04 until this morning and the only reason it moved is that a human asked what the phase was blocked on. THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT BOOKKEEPING. review means a result is out for verification, and for four of these five nothing is out and nothing ever was, while the code they describe is already merged and being built on. This is the same class as TASK-371 -- state that claims an activity nobody is performing -- but on the verification column rather than the dispatch one, and it is worse because the board's own reviewer-of-last-resort, the linter, is looking the other way. Suggested shape: a review-parked-without-verdict finding, aged, so a row that has been at review for N days with no verdict block naming it is reported. The threshold belongs beside review_fail_rounds_before_escalation in schema thresholds.

NONE of TASK-336, TASK-341, TASK-356 or TASK-357 has a spec file -- checked for evidence/*/TASK-NNN-spec.md, all four absent -- and none carries a populated verification field on its task record; the summary describes the DEFECT, not the acceptance bar. So the backlog is not four dispatches waiting to be sent, it is four rows with no bar to judge against, and writing that bar now means writing it with the implementation already visible, which is the weaker form of the negotiation-with-the-result problem that section warns about. THE ROWS DID NOT SKIP A STEP THAT EXISTED. perry-task add takes --deliverable and --verification and the store keeps no deliverable field at all, so nothing carried them to the reviewer. THAT is why this compounds rather than duplicates: a parked-without-verdict check would fire on all four and none of them could be discharged by dispatching a round. WHAT THE FIX MUST COVER, both halves: a review-parked-without-verdict finding, aged, with its threshold beside review_fail_rounds_before_escalation in schema thresholds; AND criteria captured at the point the row is opened or the work dispatched, so that finding names something a reviewer can actually be sent to judge. title: add --kr creates a linkage drift no tool can clear, because perry-goals link decides already-linked from the store and the drift is in the document
from: REPRODUCED ON LIVE STATE 2026-09-07, MINUTES AFTER ROW D AND ROW F MERGED, by filing TASK-382 with --kr and then trying to clear the warning the way row D's own result says to. Row D's agent flagged this shape in advance and got one word wrong: it wrote that every add --kr "leaves a standing linkage-store-drift warning ONLY perry-goals link can clear". perry-goals link CANNOT clear it. THE SEQUENCE, all on main: perry-task add ... --kr P003-O3-KR2 wrote the edge into linkage.jsonl, taking the store to 122 records; perry-lint then reported "P003-O3-KR2 differs between the store and phase/003-linkage.md ... the document is the stale side"; and perry-goals link TASK-382 P003-O3-KR2 answered "nothing to write -- TASK-382 is already linked to P003-O3-KR2" and wrote nothing. It is right about the STORE and the drift is about the DOCUMENT: grep -c TASK-382 phase/003-linkage.md returns 0, and the KR's tasks list there still ends at TASK-281. SO THE DRIFT IS UNCLEARABLE BY ANY TOOL PERRY HAS. WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN ONE WARNING: this phase's Objective 1 is that every declared store gets a drift verdict, and TASK-278 round 2 was just merged to make the linkage verdict REAL rather than deferred. A store that drifts permanently and by design turns that verdict back into noise -- the next real drift arrives in a column that has been reading "1 row(s) drifted" for weeks, which is the failure mode a green-by-default check always has. AND IT GROWS: one more row per add --kr, forever, until this is closed. TWO RESOLUTIONS AND THEY ARE NOT EXCLUSIVE. (A) Row E, TASK-280, is the design's own answer -- phase/<NNN>-linkage.md sheds its schema'd half, so there is no document list left to drift against. (B) perry-goals link should decide "already linked" from the DOCUMENT it writes rather than from the store it does not, so the tool row D pointed at actually discharges what add --kr creates. (B) is the smaller fix and keeps the drift clearable during whatever interval (A) takes.

title: summary is mandatory to write, reported by the linter, published by one payload and not the other, and declared in no schema
summary: perry-task add refuses a row without a summary and perry-explain is built on it, but perry-state's board payload omits the key entirely on all 145 rows while perry-task list carries it on 133, and schema/state-schema.json never mentions the field. A consumer following SKILL.md's instruction to read perry-state cannot see a field the writer will not let a row exist without.

title: D009 step 3 — the O-1 mint and the write-back to the store
to: An Objective has no durable id today, so every link to one is a guess against its title text. This step mints the id and writes it back into the store, per DESIGN-009 decisions 1 to 3. It deliberately follows step 2's byte-for-byte render gate: minting an id into a record shape that cannot rebuild OKR.md would fasten the id to the wrong thing.

title: D009 step 4 — okr.objectives[].id is filled from the store and the contract moves to 2.2
to: With ids minted, okr.objectives[].id stops being absent and is filled from the store, and the published contract moves to 2.2 with its Not here section rewritten. Done when a consumer can address an Objective by id out of the payload instead of matching its title text.

title: D009 step 5 — an Objective id survives a rename and a reorder, proved
to: The two tests that decide whether DESIGN-009 achieved anything: rename an Objective's title, and reorder the headings, and its id must be unchanged both times. An id that does not survive those two edits is a second name rather than an address, which is the defect the whole design exists to remove.

title: D010 step 4 — the scout, run by hand on ten real rows and scored against what the PMO actually decided
to: DESIGN-010's gate, and the reason step 5 may not simply follow. The scout is run by hand on ten real rows and its specs and refusals are scored against what the PMO actually decided for those same rows on 2026-08-21, which is recorded. If the scout would have dispatched a row the PMO refused, the design is wrong and the loop is not built.

title: D010 step 5 — autopilot becomes the two-stage scout-then-build loop
to: Autopilot becomes the two-stage scout-then-build loop, and this runs only if TASK-188's refusals were judged right. It is the payoff of DESIGN-010 and is deliberately the last thing built, because a loop that dispatches from bad specs is worse than one that dispatches nothing.

title: D011 step 1 — a question bank for the first-ever-OKR route
to: A question bank for the first-ever-OKR route only, with no routing and no escape hatch, to prove the shape on one path before it grows. It replaces the ten-field checklist that OKR setting is today, which collects answers without ever challenging the premise behind them.

title: D011 step 2 — a real transcript, scored by the rubric that stays unchanged
to: DESIGN-011's gate. Run the bank against a project that has no OKR.md and score the transcript with the rubric, which stays unchanged so the score cannot be negotiated. The design's third goal is measured here or it is not measured at all: if a bank-produced OKR still trips three rubric checks, the questions are wrong and steps 3 to 5 are decoration.

title: D011 step 3 — routing and smart-skip, by track spine
to: Routing and smart-skip by track spine, per DESIGN-011 decision 1, so a project that already has goals is never asked the first-ever-OKR questions. It lands after the gate, because routing a bank that produces bad OKRs only spreads them.

title: D011 step 4 — the escape hatch and the premise challenge
to: The escape hatch and the premise challenge, per DESIGN-011 decisions 2 and 4. The hatch lets a user who already knows their goal leave the interview; the challenge is what makes this an elicitation rather than a form, because a bank that never pushes back is a checklist with more steps.

title: D011 step 5 — plan-phase uses the same question bank
to: plan-phase stops carrying its own questions and reuses the same bank, per DESIGN-011 decision 3. Done when the phase interview and the OKR interview cannot drift apart, because there is one bank and not two.

title: a new queue row is born in the second stage, not the first
to: The intake track declares its stages as new, triaged, in_progress and resolved, but no row is ever born in the first of them: all 43 intake rows on this board sit at triaged and none at new. Either routing skips a stage the register declares, or the declared first stage is dead and should not be in the register at all.

title: perry-decide guards a line break with a third, weaker spelling
to: perry-decide carries its own weaker spelling of the one line-break rule. Its guard tests whether the value has more than one splitlines() element, which a TRAILING newline passes because that call returns a single element for it, while the canonical line_break_at in viewer/tables.py catches it. The comment above the guard records that the pipe half of the same paragraph was fixed two rounds earlier and this half was not.

title: The dispatch-limiter test is load-sensitive, so any row that adds work to the suite trips it
from: V4 REVIEW. Merged, and I re-ran tests.test_host_support three times on the now-quiet machine: OK, OK, OK. THE HYPOTHESIS HELD AND THE MECHANISM IS EXACT: under load the losers exit 2, LOCK TIMEOUT, not 1, cap refusal -- THEY NEVER REACH THE CAP CHECK. Idle, all 17 losers are refused by the cap; under 16 burners, 17 to 19 are refused by the LOCK. So 'winners == 3' was never asserting the cap at all; it was asserting that all 20 contenders won the lock race inside LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT. THE TWO-WAY DECISION THE USER ASKED FOR, SETTLED WITH ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN PREFERENCE: one UNCONTENDED critical section costs 0.251s idle and 5.699s median / 11.833s max under load -- a 23x blow-up, because it shells out about ten times. Serialising 20 contenders therefore needs at least 114 SECONDS of lock budget against the 10 shipped, and the required budget SCALES WITH AMBIENT LOAD while a single critical section already exceeds the timeout. So NO FINITE RETRY BUDGET MAKES THE EXACT COUNT A PROMISE -- it only moves the load at which the test flips. Fix the assertion; do not add a retry. AND IT IS NOT A BARE <=: the new form is winners == min(cap, decided) over contenders that actually reached the cap check. Exact at any load, and it pins the decided-below-cap case too, so it cannot pass by everyone losing. A REAL PREVIOUSLY-UNREPRODUCED RACE IN bin/perry-dispatch-limit, section 5 of the result: a process that won mkdir has its lock directory removed underneath it before it writes owner, surfacing as 'mv: No such file or directory' and, through set -e, EXIT 1 -- INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A CAP REFUSAL. Six anomalies in eight rounds. THAT is what TASK-313's own title describes, so it is TASK-313's first concrete reproduction. IT ALSO CAUGHT ITSELF: its first attempt reintroduced the very bug it was fixing, by adding an assertion that counted those anomalous exit-1s as cap refusals; it went red immediately and is recorded in section 6. HONEST LIMIT, STATED NOT HIDDEN: under heavy load the contended test cannot detect an off-by-one cap. But the OLD assertion was red 6 of 6 at base under that load, so it detected nothing either -- and test_global_cap_still_wins is serial and stays red on that mutation under load. Serial tests own the arithmetic; contended tests own the race. MACHINE COST, section 10: about 45 to 60 minutes of oversubscription, burners tagged PERRYBURNER so they are countable rather than inferred, and all verified dead. It stopped the broad census after one run and traded it for a targeted measurement. Its stated constraint: this verification method is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE WITH PARALLEL DISPATCH -- and note the machine sat at load 109-121 from four OTHER agents with none of its burners running, so its 'idle' baseline was never truly idle.

title: A board-render test breaks whenever a row's prose contains its sentinel word
from: V4 REVIEW. Merged; test_board_render is green on main and the only red is gone. THE DEFECT WAS SCOPE, NOT status, AND THE CENSUS PROVED IT BEFORE THE FIX WENT IN. 7 fields carry sentinels; 3 of those sentinels are ordinary words prose produces; and TWO ALREADY COLLIDE ON TODAY'S BOARD across 145 rendered rows -- 'dropped' for status and 'Nobody' for owner. I confirmed both counts independently: 'dropped' appears 8 times in BOARD.md and 'Nobody' once, every occurrence in Title or Next action. So 'Nobody' was ONE BOARD ROW from firing, and fixing status alone would have left it loaded -- which is exactly what the row predicted and why the census was made a required deliverable rather than a nicety. The third, 'V6' for verification, is a token this project writes routinely ('closes at V4') and collides the day a V6 exists. THE SHAPE IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I PROPOSED. I suggested asserting on the cell instead of the row. The round did that AND replaced absence with EQUALITY AGAINST THE CELL AS IT RENDERED BEFORE THE MUTATION, because scoping alone leaves a residual: a row whose Status column legitimately HOLDS the sentinel would still fail an assertNotIn. Equality also grades strictly more -- a renderer that blanked the cell to an em dash on restore satisfies assertNotIn and fails equality -- and a new assertNotEqual precondition stops the round trip going vacuous. The column resolves by NAME through the schema glossary rather than by fixed index, because column order is not schema-constrained. ONE CLAIM I COULD NOT CONFIRM AND AM NOT REPEATING AS FACT: the round says USER-916 currently renders status: dropped, making the sentinel a value the graded column legitimately takes. USER-916 does not appear as a row in BOARD.md's task table on main, so I could not reproduce that. The reviewer should settle it -- if true it strengthens the equality argument; if false the argument still stands on the two measured collisions. ONE GREEN, KEPT AND DEMOTED RATHER THAN DELETED OR OVERSOLD: E1 shows the restore half has no independent power -- stripping the set half and running the restore half alone against a real mutation comes back green, because BOARD.md is a static template here so the only stale value a renderer can hold IS the board's original text, and the set half fails on it one assertion earlier. It is kept, because dropping it is wrong and it is the only assertion checking both directions, but it is now recorded as never having been shown to catch anything. IT ALSO REFUTED ITS OWN HYPOTHESIS: it predicted the old whole-row rule would PASS one mutation, which would have made cell scoping strictly stronger at catching bugs. It does not -- it goes red on all seven fields. So that claim is not made. What cell scoping fixes is the FALSE RED, not a false green. Suite: 3 consecutive runs, 114 modules / 3257 tests, all green each time.

title: every NS-01 warning Perry emits is about a file Perry itself wrote, and the remedy each one offers is a no-op
from: From the 2026-09-02 design-register audit, finding L-01. DESIGN-002 section 5 makes a specific promise about how the collision check decides, and the implementation does not keep it: all five live warnings are Perry's own output in directories Perry claims and writes. The remedy text compounds it -- every warning says 'move Perry's state to its own root, /perry relocate perry', and the state root IS perry/, so the one action offered is a no-op. One of the five is a separate bug: perry/intake.jsonl is a FILE claim and the warning tells the reader to 'move these files out of intake.jsonl'. ADR-011 measured this population at 0:4 signal-to-noise and left lint's namespace half on the delete list on that basis; it is 0:5 now, and the characterisation was charitable -- these are not files a user placed. NOTE FOR THE PMO READING THIS LATER: this is why every lint run today reported '4 warnings' or '5 warnings' and every session skipped them as pre-existing. A check that only ever cries wolf gets trained out of the reader.
to: REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-09-07 BY WRITING ONE FILE THE DOCUMENTED WAY. The PMO wrote a knowledge card at knowledge/verification/, which is exactly where work/SKILL.md says knowledge digests live, and perry-lint went from "knowledge/ holds 3 file(s) Perry did not write" to 4 in the same run. So the count is not a legacy of some import: it grows by one every time somebody uses the mechanism as documented. THE SECOND HALF, AND IT IS THE SHARPER ONE: knowledge/INDEX.md still reads "Active: 0 · Eternal: 0 · Stale: 0 · Archived: 0" and "(no digests yet)" while four cards sit beside it. The index calls itself "Auto-maintained by the work lane, updated on every digest, archive operation, and full rebuild during end-phase-retro" -- and nothing maintains it. That is WHY the NS-01 fires: the files are real, the index that would claim them is empty, so Perry reads its own knowledge directory as somebody else's folder. WHY THE OFFERED REMEDY IS A NO-OP HERE, concretely: the warning tells the user to run /perry relocate perry, and the state root ALREADY IS perry -- the files are at perry/knowledge/verification/. Relocating cannot move a file out of a directory it is already correctly inside. The same is true of the phase/ warning, which names seven snapshots score-phase itself writes. SO THE ROW'S CLAIM IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: on this project every NS-01 names files Perry wrote or told a user to write -- 7 phase snapshots, 4 knowledge cards -- and the remedy is inapplicable to all eleven. TASK-222 is the phase/ half of the same defect. The fix probably has two parts, an index that is actually maintained and a claim check that consults it, and this row should say which part it owns before it is dispatched.
