from: REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-09-07, 17 days after this row was filed, and the reproduction is that the defect FORCED A CHOICE BETWEEN TWO FALSEHOODS. Recording a re-measurement on P003-O2-KR1 required editing phase/003-linkage.md and running "perry-tasks linkage-write --from-register". Bumping the register's "updated:" field from 2026-09-03T06:06:45Z to today, which is what recording a fresh measurement means, REWROTE "declared_at" ON ALL 115 edge AND unlinked RECORDS to today -- 115 records silently claiming they were declared in an action that never happened. Reverting "updated:" restored every "declared_at" to the truth and left the store differing from its pre-edit state by EXACTLY ONE FIELD, the "current: 0" that was the point. VERIFIED BY DIFF BOTH WAYS, not by reading the code. THE CHOICE THE DEFECT FORCES: bump "updated" and 115 provenance dates become false, or leave it and perry-state reports the fresh measurement as STALE -- which is what P003-O1-KR2 and P003-O2-KR1 both now show, both wrongly, because the measurement is from today. I took the second, because a stale flag is a visible wrong answer and a re-dated declaration is an invisible one. THE FIX SHAPE IS NOW OBVIOUS FROM THE REPRODUCTION: "declared_at" must be carried per record rather than derived from the register's file-level "updated", so the two facts the field conflates -- when this register was last touched, and when THIS edge was declared -- stop sharing one slot. A pipe-written tasks value declares an edge the reader silently drops, because the id carries a trailing newline and the match is exact
from: FOUND BY TASK-278 ROUND 3 WHILE ENUMERATING THE REGISTER SHAPES, and it is the one shape in that enumeration where the answer is wrong rather than merely unlocated. A block scalar value -- tasks: written with a pipe -- parses to a single string carrying its trailing newline, so the value is a list of one element whose text is the id plus a newline. kr_for_task matches the id EXACTLY, so it never matches that element, and the READER silently drops the edge. A register written that way declares an edge that nothing in Perry honours: the KR does not count it, attribution does not see it, and no check says a declaration was lost. CONSISTENT WITH purge AND THAT IS THE POINT, not a mitigation: the guard and the reader agree the edge is not there, so nothing reports a disagreement, which is exactly the shape that makes a silent loss silent. Round 3's guard work does not change it, because the guard's job is to protect a row the register names and this register names nothing the reader can resolve. WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY rather than folded into round 3: round 3's Bound is about which shapes the purge GUARD locates, and this is about which shapes the linkage READER resolves. Same enumeration, different consumer, and the fix is in the reader or in a lint refusal, not in the guard. WHAT TO DECIDE: whether a pipe-written tasks value should be refused at lint time as a shape the register may not use, or normalised by the reader so the edge resolves. Refusing is smaller and matches how the register treats the other shapes it cannot honour; normalising is friendlier and adds a second place where an id's exact characters are decided. Check first whether perry-goals link can ever WRITE that shape -- if it cannot, refusing costs nobody anything.
to: SEVERITY CORRECTED 2026-09-08, AND THE CORRECTION IS TO WHAT THE PMO WROTE ON THIS ROW. This row said a pipe-written tasks value declares an edge that is dropped SILENTLY, with no KR counting it, no attribution seeing it, and NO CHECK REPORTING IT MISSING. THE LAST CLAUSE IS FALSE. Found by TASK-278 round 3's V4 and reproduced by the PMO: planting `tasks: |` with the id on the following line draws a HARD LINT ERROR -- "perry/phase/002-linkage.md [bad-type] objectives[2].krs[1].tasks must be a list" -- so the register is refused outright rather than accepted with a lost edge. WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND IS WHY THE ROW SURVIVES: the READER still drops the edge. kr_for_task matches the id exactly and the block scalar yields the id plus a trailing newline, so the two halves disagree about the same input -- the linter calls the register malformed while the reader silently returns one fewer edge for it. A register in that state is refused by one tool and half-honoured by another, which is a smaller defect than a silent loss but is still two answers to one question. SO THE ROW IS NO LONGER ABOUT DATA LOSS. It is about a shape that fails a type check and, independently, resolves to nothing in a reader that never consults that check. Whoever takes it should decide whether the reader should refuse in the same terms the linter does, or whether being refused at lint time is sufficient and the reader's behaviour is unreachable in practice -- and MEASURE which, rather than assume, because the linter is not on every path that loads a register. DOWNGRADED FROM P1 TO P2 ON THAT BASIS. The original P1 rested on the silence, and the silence is not there.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS ON THE PHASE, NOT ON A TOOL. Definition of Done item 5, as restated 2026-08-31, reads: every main-track row opened after the gate lands carries A KR EDGE OR AN UNLINKED DECLARATION WRITTEN BY ITS OWN add. The second half has no implementation, so a row that genuinely serves no KR CANNOT satisfy item 5 the way item 5 describes it. Its only available action is to omit --kr, which the computation counts as not-answered and puts in the denominator. SO EVERY HONEST no-KR ROW PERMANENTLY LOWERS THIS KR, and the 100 percent target is unreachable by construction rather than by not having done the work yet. THIS IS WHY THE NUMBER LOOKS THE WAY IT DOES. P003-O3-KR2 read 50 percent, then 33, then 15.38, and none of those moves was a regression -- the denominator grew as rows were filed and most of them legitimately serve no KR. The KR is measuring honestly and the target it is measured against cannot be reached. TWO RESOLUTIONS AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT. (A) GIVE add A WRITER for the declaration: a row can say at add time that it serves no KR, producing kind unlinked with via add, and it then counts as ANSWERED. This is what DoD item 5 already describes and it makes the 100 percent target reachable. (B) RESTATE THE KR so that omitting --kr counts as answered-with-none. Cheaper, but it destroys the distinction the KR exists to measure -- never-asked and declared-no-KR become the same reading, which is exactly the state DESIGN-015 section 5.2 built the derivation to tell apart. THE PMO RECOMMENDS (A), and the reason is that (B) makes the number un-interpretable rather than merely lower: after (B) a KR at 100 percent would tell you nothing about whether anybody was ever asked. DESIGN-016 Decision 1 — how the standup gets a small structured read. MEASURED 2026-09-04 on 5d19d83: SKILL.md:130 mandates perry-state --json every invocation and that payload is 186,856 bytes (~47k tokens) on this repository; its largest section, board, is 122,828 on its own; the only compact answer, --dashboard, is 1,132 bytes and text-only. perry-context-budget reports 99.1% of this project's 8.43B tokens is context re-read per turn, so this is the expensive kind of cost. A: add a --compact payload derived in-process from the full one and point SKILL.md step 3 at it (recommended — --json keeps its published shape, and the narrow mode can be tested as a strict projection). B: add --fields selection instead, so the caller names what it wants (more flexible, but every caller now has to know the field names). C: change nothing in the tool and narrow SKILL.md to a list of --section calls (cheapest, but board alone is still 31k tokens, so it does not reach the goal).
answer: 决定 2026-09-08：选 A —— 新增 --compact payload，从完整 payload 在进程内派生。--json 保持已发布的形状不变，所以 aiMark 和任何现有消费者不受影响，而窄模式可以作为一个严格投影来测试。重新测量后这个决定比立项时更紧迫：payload 从 09-04 的 186,856 bytes 涨到今天的 258,989 bytes（约 65k tokens），+39%，其中 board 一个 section 占 159,648 bytes = 72%。涨的是本会话加的十几行 task。第一手证据：今天开场跑 perry-state --json 输出 248.8KB 被系统直接转存到文件，因为塞不进上下文，此后整个会话都在从那个文件里抠字段。选项 C（只改 SKILL.md 用 --section）明确排除：board 单独就是 72%，达不到目标。

title: DESIGN-016 Decision 2 — where the --help rationale goes. MEASURED 2026-09-04: perry-task answers --help with 160 lines / 10,059 bytes and its Usage block starts at line 51; perry-lint 135 lines, perry-goals 106, and four more tools put Usage past line 36. The prose above the fold is ADR numbers, the bug that motivated the tool and why each refusal is a refusal — it is good content and it is not what a caller asking for a flag list wants first. A: usage-first --help, rationale behind --help --verbose (recommended — nothing is lost and the default call gets cheap). B: move the rationale into bin/README.md and leave only usage in the tool (README is already 20KB and would grow). C: leave as-is and accept the ~2.5k token discovery cost per tool.
answer: 决定 2026-09-08：选 B —— 论证搬进 bin/README.md，--help 只留 Usage 和子命令。重新测量：perry-task --help 169 行 10,690 字节，Usage 在第 51 行；perry-goals 107 行，Usage 在第 58 行；perry-decide 62 行，Usage 在第 41 行。而 perry-lint 同样长（136 行）Usage 却在第 8 行，说明这不是论证太多，是排版顺序。PMO 提出的风险，用户已知并接受：论证离开它解释的代码之后两边会各自漂移，而那正是 ADR-019 今天删掉的那一类重复。缓解办法应与搬迁同批交付，不是后补：bin/README.md 目前覆盖 19 个工具中的 19 个，但没有任何测试引用它，覆盖是手工维持的。搬迁应带一个机械检查——每个 bin/ 工具在 README 里有对应小节，且其 Usage 块与工具实际的 --help 一致——把漂移从静默变成被报告，这是 perry-lint 对其它投影已经在用的模式。

title: Dispatched agents are handed a worktree 496 commits behind main, and a stale base produces work that looks correct
from: Three of the four agents dispatched on 2026-09-07 were given a worktree checked out at a 2026-09-02 commit rather than at current main. Each noticed independently and recovered differently, at its own cost. The danger is not the wasted time: a spec's line numbers were measured against that same stale ref, so work built on it matches its spec, passes its own tests, and is wrong about the tree it merges into.
to: Three of the four agents dispatched on 2026-09-07 were given a worktree checked out at a 2026-09-02 commit rather than at current main. Each noticed independently and recovered differently, at its own cost. The danger is not the wasted time: a spec's line numbers were measured against that same stale ref, so work built on it matches its spec, passes its own tests, and is wrong about the tree it merges into. REPRODUCED AGAIN 2026-09-10, and the number grew: three review agents dispatched for the DESIGN-016 V4 round were all handed d49964ee, the SAME 2026-09-02 commit as the four on 2026-09-07, now 653 commits behind the branch tip rather than 496. The subject of the review was absent from the tree -- zero of the six SURFACE-declaring tools existed, and the acceptance criteria file did not either. All three stopped at the base gate and produced no verdict, which cost three full dispatches to learn a SHA. THE GATE ONLY WORKED BECAUSE THE DISPATCH PROMPT CARRIED IT: each prompt named the required SHA and said stop if it differs. Nothing in the harness checks this, so a round dispatched without that paragraph would have reviewed a tree with no subject in it. The stale ref is not drifting -- it is pinned at d49964ee across two independent dispatch events eight days apart, which points at a fixed ref rather than a race. The PMO workaround, and the thing to compare a fix against: git worktree add --detach <path> <sha> from the primary checkout, then dispatch a non-isolated agent with that path and an explicit ban on touching the shared checkout.

title: the declaration is checked both ways on perry-task alone; the other five tools are unguarded in both directions
summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 4, DESIGN-016, AND REPRODUCED ON ALL SIX TOOLS AT ONCE. Direction B -- a flag SURFACE declares that no code reads -- was planted on all six tools in one mutation and 3440 tests stayed at baseline. perry-task start --rung V4 exits 0, prints 'wrote TASK-001 (start)' and stores rung=None: the accepted-and-silently-dropped defect DESIGN-016 section 1.4 says the declaration was bought to remove. Direction A -- code reads a flag the declaration does not carry -- is guarded on perry-task only, by an AST walk; dropping --wip from perry-config track's declared flags while bin/perry-config:289 still reads it left the suite at baseline, which is the round-1 regression shape reproducible today. THE GUARD THAT EXISTED IS A HAND-WRITTEN TABLE OF TEN (tool, sub, flag) ROWS AT tests/test_bin_surface.py ELSEWHERE, against a negative space the same reviewer measured at 1277 pairs. 134afea6 closed BOTH directions for perry-task by inverting the AST walk already there, and left the other five because each has a different dispatch shape: perry-tasks and perry-config are if-chains, perry-okr runs perry_md_store whose flags are declared in a FUNCTION rather than a literal, and perry-state and perry-diagnose declare zero subcommands so their direction-B question is tool-level rather than per-subcommand. WHAT THE REVIEWER ALSO ESTABLISHED, so this row need not re-derive it: the negative space is clean today -- 1277 probes, 0 accepted -- so this is a guard against tomorrow, not a live defect. perry-config track --mode specifically is intact.

title: the contract page's rule-3 snippet compares minors as strings, so a consumer is warned about older changes and blind to newer ones
summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 4, DESIGN-016. TWO DEFECTS IN ONE SNIPPET, BOTH LATENT AND BOTH DOCUMENTATION-ONLY, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A FAIL. (1) change['version'] > TESTED_MINOR_STR is a STRING compare, so '1.5' > '1.18' is true and a consumer pinned at 1.18 is warned about an OLDER change -- the exact comparison the page's own semantics[].version row warns against, 'never as a float', string compare working only 'against the same-shaped string'. (2) if (major, minor) > max(SUPPORTED) with SUPPORTED = {(1,18),(2,0)} makes any 1.x minor drift unreportable, because (1,19) > (2,0) is false. NOTHING EXECUTES THE SNIPPET. The reviewer DID execute the OTHER snippet on that page -- the rule-1 version gate -- and it is correct: it accepts 2.0 against a live payload, accepts 1.18, rejects 3.0. So the page is half-verified and this is the unverified half. The tool ships 2.0, so no consumer is being misled today. RELATED: the changelog guard on the same page was wrong until 2ba2c565 (range(minor+1) demanded twenty headings at 1.19 and one at 2.0) and round 4 confirmed the no-gaps-per-major replacement with four independent mutations, all red.

title: bound.open_total and bound.closed_total are published to dashboards and asserted by nothing
summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 4, DESIGN-016. grep -rn 'open_total|closed_total' tests/ returns NOTHING across 3440 tests. Setting open_total = total makes perry-task list report open_total 404 / closed_total 0 on a store that is truly 156/248, print the wrong figure on stderr too, and leave the whole suite at baseline. NOT A FAIL and the reviewer was right not to call it one: the values are correct at HEAD, and neither DESIGN-016 goal 6 nor the round's criterion 6 names them -- criterion 6 asks that the payload SAY how many rows exist beyond the bound, which bound.total and bound.truncated do and which ARE asserted. But schema/task-list-contract.md tells dashboards to render exactly these two fields, so a regression here is consumer-visible and silent.

summary: COST TWO OF THREE V4 REVIEWERS A DETOUR ON 2026-09-10 AND WILL COST THE NEXT ONE THE SAME. tests/test_resume.py TestStaleRuns.test_a_fresh_run_is_not_stale is red and pre-existing: it is byte-identical at 4ebc0693 and one reviewer confirmed it red there by extracting that commit with git archive, the other by re-running it alone. a computed KR publishes current with no target, so the best-measured row in the register renders as unwritten
summary: ASKED BY AIMARK 2026-09-09, reading perry-goals/list/3.0 against Perry's own project, and the consequence is visible on their page. P003-O3-KR2 is the most rigorously measured row in the register -- bin/lib section same_action_linkage recomputes it from linkage.jsonl and .perry/events.jsonl on every read, current 43.333333333333336, provenance measured with numerator 13 and denominator 30 -- and it is the ONLY row aiMark shows nothing for, because it draws a bar only when target and current are both numbers. That is Perry's own rule: contract 2.0 removed progress because Perry cannot tell which direction a KR runs, and the contract page says only the consumer draws the bar. So aiMark obeys and displays nothing. Phase objective O3 has exactly this one KR, so it renders as 'nobody wrote down what done would mean' beside a number Perry recomputes from two event logs on every read, next to O1 at 100%. THE TARGET EXISTS AND IS PROSE: the first three words of metric are 'Target 100%.' AIMARK OFFERED TWO SHAPES AND SAID IT CANNOT PICK, BECAUSE PICKING IS INFERRING: (a) target 100, current stays a percentage, additive, a minor; (b) target 30 / current 13, the count form every other phase KR uses, but it retypes what current MEANS on this row and needs a semantics entry. THE PMO RECOMMENDS (a), ON A FACT AIMARK DID NOT HAVE: this KR's denominator is not fixed. same_action_linkage computes it as 'the rows that were asked' -- the main-track rows whose own add event carries a kr key -- so it GROWS every time a row is opened during phase 003. Under (b) the target would move under the KR, and a target that changes when someone opens a row is a denominator, not a target. The other phase KRs are counts because their targets are fixed counts (6 stores declared); this one is not the same shape. Under (a) the target is 100 and fixed, which is what was authored, and the moving denominator stays where it belongs, in current_measurement. ONE THING TO SETTLE WHILE DOING IT: 43.333333333333336 is float noise in a published payload; decide the precision and say it on the page.

title: a hand-measured zero and a template zero nobody touched are the same payload, and asserted_at empty is the whole signal
summary: ASKED BY AIMARK 2026-09-09. CONFIRMED BY THE PMO AGAINST THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN AGREED: current_provenance.state is a TWO-VALUED vocabulary, asserted / unasserted, with measured as a separate boolean, and schema/goals-list-contract.md line 143 documents asserted_at empty as 'a real state and not an error: nobody wrote the date down'. So there is no third state available and the empty date is indeed the whole signal. THE CASE AIMARK BUILT IT ON: P003-O2-KR1 carries target 0, current 0, provenance asserted with measured false and asserted_at empty. Its metric prose says the number was measured by hand on 2026-09-07 and shows the grep that produced it, so the zero is real and hard-won -- and the payload's account of it is byte-identical to what a zero nobody ever touched looks like. THIS IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE DEFECT CONTRACT 2.1 ALREADY NAMED AND ONLY HALF-CLOSED. 2.1's note says the register template pre-fills current 0 so a drive-to-zero KR 'reads as achieved on the day it is written', and P002-O2-KR2 did exactly that; current_provenance and current_staleness shipped as the answer. They answer 'is this number stale' and they do not answer 'did anyone ever write this number'. The contract page even says an ABSENT current is null and unasserted, never 0 -- which is the right rule and is not what the template does. WHAT AIMARK DID ON ITS OWN SIDE, so this row does not re-litigate it: krProgress used to return null on any zero target to dodge a division; it now reads target 0 with current 0 as MET, because two numbers were stated and they agree, which is the same reading as target 3 current 3 and not a division at all. A zero target with a NON-zero current still returns null deliberately -- a count that went from four to one is three quarters done only if you know it started at four, and that baseline lives in metric prose. If Perry wants that bar drawn, the baseline has to become a field.

title: TASK-361 was closed on a V4 PASS whose test could not have failed for 8 of the 41 writing subcommands
summary: A CLOSED ROW WHOSE VERIFICATION DID NOT VERIFY, FOUND BY V4 ROUND 5 AND NOT BY THE ROUND THAT CLOSED IT. TASK-361 is DESIGN-016 A3, --dry-run and --json on every writer. Round 4 PASSed it and the PMO closed it at V4 on 2026-09-10. Round 5 then disabled the dry-run gate at bin/perry-tasks:234 and the FULL suite stayed green while perry-tasks write --from-board --dry-run rewrote its store and printed 'wrote'; the same at bin/perry-config:117 rewrote .perry/config.jsonl while printing 'Nothing was written'. The test round 4 relied on, test_dry_run_changes_no_bytes_anywhere, minted every store in setUp and then compared bytes -- so the non-dry-run twin was a byte no-op and the comparison could not distinguish a dry run from a real one for 8 of the 41 writing subcommands. Its reached>=2 guard counted commands that EXITED 0, not commands that would have changed bytes. THE GAP IS ALREADY CLOSED IN CODE, 1789af8a: each command now disturbs its own side first and carries its own control, and perry-config gained the dry-run sweep it never had. Both mutations are red. SO THIS ROW IS BOOKKEEPING, NOT WORK -- and it is filed rather than fixed silently because the PMO closed a row on a verification that did not hold, and the board currently says TASK-361 passed V4 without saying what that PASS covered. A SECOND DISCREPANCY THE SAME REVIEWER FOUND: the criteria file's row map assigns criterion 4 to TASK-361, and round 5's dispatch routed criterion 4a to TASK-360, so the finding was charged to TASK-360's verdict. Whoever reconciles this should make the two agree.

title: Is the bin/ tool boundary drawn on the mechanism or on the object? DESIGN-016 section 8 asks it, section 1.4 is the evidence, and Decision 3 explicitly did not rule on it. Four registers -- tasks, risks, intake, asks -- are each named twice, once by perry-task for their lane verbs and once by perry-tasks for their store verbs, in two tools that differ by one letter and disagree about singular/plural and about which side the verb goes on. Option A: keep the mechanism split as it is, and TASK-066's per-subcommand-group split of perry-task proceeds. Option B: redraw by object, one tool per register holding both its lane and store verbs, which makes TASK-066's split the wrong cut. Option C: neither now -- record the axis as decided-to-defer with a date, so it stops blocking. THIS IS A BREAKING CHANGE TO EVERY CALL SITE in the skill and in every project already using Perry, which is why DESIGN-016 section 1.4 calls itself a finding and not a proposal, and why it is the user's call rather than a task. NOT COSTED ANYWHERE YET: no one has measured how many call sites a rename touches.

title: Is the bin/ tool boundary drawn on the mechanism or on the object? Supersedes USER-922, which listed three options and was missing the one the PMO recommends. THE PROBLEM, in one sentence: there are two tools one letter apart -- perry-task writes rows the way you work every day, perry-tasks rebuilds and compares the stores behind them -- and to pick one you must know which KIND of operation you want before you can say WHICH THING you want it done to. The four things are tasks, risks, intake and asks. OPTION A -- leave it. TASK-066's per-subcommand-group split of perry-task then proceeds. OPTION B -- one tool per thing: perry-risk holds both its everyday verbs and its repair verbs. This is what DESIGN-016 section 8 asks. Costs 475 live call sites plus 623 in bin/, 200 in tests, 56 in viewer/, and every project already using Perry; the 4589 mentions in journal and evidence are history and must not be touched. OPTION C -- decide to defer, with a date, so it stops blocking TASK-066. OPTION D, RECOMMENDED BY THE PMO -- keep the two tools and let BOTH take the thing as a parameter. C5 already did this on the repair side: risks-build became perry-tasks build --register risks, with the register list read from schema section claims and the twelve old names kept as aliases for one release. The everyday side still spells the thing into the verb -- risk-add, intake-sweep, ask, answer -- eight subcommands. Finishing the same move there makes both tools symmetric and costs eight subcommands plus aliases instead of a rename. TWO FACTS THAT CHANGED THE PREMISE SINCE SECTION 1.4 WAS WRITTEN: (1) C5 already answered half the question in the object direction, so the prefix table is asymmetric because the work is half done, not because the design is confused; (2) section 1.4's complaint was that the names do not carry the distinction, and perry list and perry describe now carry it, so nobody has to read it out of a name. THE ARGUMENT FOR KEEPING THE MECHANISM SPLIT: the everyday side takes a lock, stamps an event, writes the journal and the board; the repair side does one-way imports and byte comparisons. Different risk classes. Under option B, perry-risk render --write sits one tab-completion from perry-risk add -- and render --write is the one place in this repository that was found reporting a write it had not performed.

answer: OPTION B, AND ALL THREE PAIRS. Decided by the user 2026-09-10. The reason given is architectural rather than economic: two commands that differ by one character cannot coexist, and the cost of many external references is acceptable BECAUSE AGENTS DO THE WORK -- which is the premise that makes B affordable now and did not hold when section 1.4 was written. Scope is all three pairs section 1.4 names, not just the acute one: perry-task/perry-tasks differ by 1 character, perry-state/perry-state-cost by 5, perry-goals/perry-okr are the same shape with a different word. Renaming in three passes would break downstream projects three times and each later pass would be harder to justify than the first. WHAT B MEANS CONCRETELY: the boundary is redrawn on the OBJECT. perry-task keeps tasks alone; perry-risk, perry-intake and perry-ask appear, each holding both its everyday verbs and its store verbs; perry-tasks disappears and the confusable pair goes with it. THE PMO'S RESERVATION, RECORDED AND OVERRULED: under B a destructive maintenance verb sits beside an everyday one -- perry-risk render --write next to perry-risk add -- and render --write is the one command in this repository found reporting a write it had not performed. title: a hand-measured zero and a template zero nobody touched are the same payload, and asserted_at empty is the whole signal
from: ASKED BY AIMARK 2026-09-09. CONFIRMED BY THE PMO AGAINST THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN AGREED: current_provenance.state is a TWO-VALUED vocabulary, asserted / unasserted, with measured as a separate boolean, and schema/goals-list-contract.md line 143 documents asserted_at empty as 'a real state and not an error: nobody wrote the date down'. So there is no third state available and the empty date is indeed the whole signal. THE CASE AIMARK BUILT IT ON: P003-O2-KR1 carries target 0, current 0, provenance asserted with measured false and asserted_at empty. Its metric prose says the number was measured by hand on 2026-09-07 and shows the grep that produced it, so the zero is real and hard-won -- and the payload's account of it is byte-identical to what a zero nobody ever touched looks like. THIS IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE DEFECT CONTRACT 2.1 ALREADY NAMED AND ONLY HALF-CLOSED. 2.1's note says the register template pre-fills current 0 so a drive-to-zero KR 'reads as achieved on the day it is written', and P002-O2-KR2 did exactly that; current_provenance and current_staleness shipped as the answer. They answer 'is this number stale' and they do not answer 'did anyone ever write this number'. The contract page even says an ABSENT current is null and unasserted, never 0 -- which is the right rule and is not what the template does. WHAT AIMARK DID ON ITS OWN SIDE, so this row does not re-litigate it: krProgress used to return null on any zero target to dodge a division; it now reads target 0 with current 0 as MET, because two numbers were stated and they agree, which is the same reading as target 3 current 3 and not a division at all. A zero target with a NON-zero current still returns null deliberately -- a count that went from four to one is three quarters done only if you know it started at four, and that baseline lives in metric prose. If Perry wants that bar drawn, the baseline has to become a field.

title: What independent source of truth does the --compact projection test have, and if the answer is none, where does criterion 5 stop? TASK-362 has now FAILED FOUR V4 ROUNDS -- the limit is 2 -- and perry-lint reports review-rounds-exhausted on it. FOUR ROUNDS, FOUR DIFFERENT LAYERS OF ONE SHAPE, each found only because the previous fix removed the layer above it: round 4, the RULE was verified by calling the function under test; round 5, the DATA was cardinality one so a projection keeping only the first of anything was green; round 6, the PAIRING resolved each expectation through the very path it was checking, 46 of 53 pairs repointable while green; round 7, the same pairing defect one level down in the subdict children, plus _at itself being shared by the tool and by the test's expectation. ROUND 7 NAMED THE PRINCIPLE PLAINLY AND IT IS A REAL FORK: no test in tests/test_compact_payload.py reads .perry/config.jsonl, okr.jsonl, linkage.jsonl or schema/. --json is the reference on both sides and BOTH COME FROM ONE build(). If build() is wrong, both agree and every test in the module passes. READING 1 -- the criterion's ceiling is that the projection is applied CONSISTENTLY over its whole declaration, an independent source is out of reach for a projection by definition, and the row closes when every declared pair is compared from the key: the ten subdict triples, the eleven arg names, and _at. Bounded, finite, and the fix is already specified by round 7. READING 2 -- criterion 5 says every key carries the same VALUE, so it needs a source outside build(): the store files and schema/ read independently. That is a larger piece of work and would give the module the property it has never had. THE PMO RECOMMENDS READING 1 for this row and READING 2 as a separate row, because the four rounds converged rather than diverged -- each went one level deeper and the category is now enumerated and finite -- and because the rounds-exhausted rule exists to stop a search with no last element, which this no longer is. But the rule is the rule and this is the decision it asks for. WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE regardless of the answer: criterion 13 has held under three independent rounds of attack including five directions round 7 invented, and the code has been correct at every round -- what failed each time was the evidence that it was correct.

title: perry-diagnose reads the whole board line for the word answered, so an ask whose question contains resolved counts as answered
summary: FOUND 2026-09-10 AND IT IS RED ON MAIN RIGHT NOW. bin/perry-diagnose:335 ANSWERED = re.compile(r'\b(answered|resolved|closed|done|decided|已回答|已解决|已决定)\b') is searched against the WHOLE BOARD LINE, so any of those words appearing in the QUESTION marks the ask answered. Measured on USER-924, filed today: its text contains 'round 6, the PAIRING resolved each expectation through the very path it was checking', diagnose matches 'resolved', and open_decisions_by_register.queue reports 0 while one ask is pending. THIS IS TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF ONE RULE, the shape this repository keeps finding in itself. viewer/parsers.py:2094 already has _ASK_STILL_OPEN = ('pending','waiting','open','—','-') and ask_is_answered(status_cell) at :2097, which reads the STATUS CELL. perry-diagnose does not call it and scans prose instead -- which ADR-007 decision 3 forbids in as many words: Python does not parse document semantics. IT HAS BEEN BROKEN THE WHOLE TIME AND NOTHING COULD SEE IT. The reconciliation test asserts diagnose and perry-task agree, and 0 == 0 held for weeks because every ask in the queue was answered. It went red the first time a pending ask existed. That is not a flaky test; it is a test that finally got an input. NOTE THE SECOND-ORDER RISK: the fix must not simply widen the regex. Perry-task writes 'pending' and the fixture writes 'open', and the shared predicate already knows both -- calling it is the fix; teaching a second copy the same words is how there come to be three.

summary: SELF-REPORTED BY THE AGENT THAT DID IT, 2026-09-10, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON IT IS KNOWN. Drafting specs for four rows, it redirected a baseline to scratchpad/baseline.txt while a sibling agent in scratchpad/fixA was writing the same path; on seeing the wrong tree name in the output it ran pkill -f 'tests/run'. fixA's log shows 'Terminated: 15'. THE BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN THE AGENT KNEW: ListAgents shows seven interactive peer sessions on this machine at the time, two of them other Perry sessions (perry-73, perry-84). A pattern kill on 'tests/run' reaches every session's suite, not just this one's subagents, and none of them would see a reason -- they would see a run that died. FOURTH COLLISION OF THE SAME ROOT CAUSE, all four in two days: V4 round 4's r4b and r4c both wrote scratchpad/baseline.txt and one clobbered the other mid-run; round 5 the same; round 6 the same; and now a clobber that escalated into a process kill. Three times it cost a re-measurement. This time it cost another agent's work. TWO FIXES AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT SIZES. (1) work/reference/review-constraints.md already forbids git checkout / stash / reset / clean by name, and the reasoning transfers verbatim -- each one can destroy work that is not yours and not recoverable. It does not mention signals. Add pkill, killall and kill -9, with the reason: on a shared machine a pattern kill has no way to tell your process from someone else's, and the agent that runs one cannot see who else was working. (2) The dispatch side is the actual root cause: every prompt in this session handed out one scratchpad directory and told the agent to namespace inside it, which is advice, not isolation. A private path per agent removes the collision instead of asking four agents in a row to remember.

title: What independent source of truth does the --compact projection test have, and if the answer is none, where does criterion 5 stop? TASK-362 has now FAILED FOUR V4 ROUNDS -- the limit is 2 -- and perry-lint reports review-rounds-exhausted on it. FOUR ROUNDS, FOUR DIFFERENT LAYERS OF ONE SHAPE, each found only because the previous fix removed the layer above it: round 4, the RULE was verified by calling the function under test; round 5, the DATA was cardinality one so a projection keeping only the first of anything was green; round 6, the PAIRING resolved each expectation through the very path it was checking, 46 of 53 pairs repointable while green; round 7, the same pairing defect one level down in the subdict children, plus _at itself being shared by the tool and by the test's expectation. ROUND 7 NAMED THE PRINCIPLE PLAINLY AND IT IS A REAL FORK: no test in tests/test_compact_payload.py reads .perry/config.jsonl, okr.jsonl, linkage.jsonl or schema/. --json is the reference on both sides and BOTH COME FROM ONE build(). If build() is wrong, both agree and every test in the module passes. READING 1 -- the criterion's ceiling is that the projection is applied CONSISTENTLY over its whole declaration, an independent source is out of reach for a projection by definition, and the row closes when every declared pair is compared from the key: the ten subdict triples, the eleven arg names, and _at. Bounded, finite, and the fix is already specified by round 7. READING 2 -- criterion 5 says every key carries the same VALUE, so it needs a source outside build(): the store files and schema/ read independently. That is a larger piece of work and would give the module the property it has never had. THE PMO RECOMMENDS READING 1 for this row and READING 2 as a separate row, because the four rounds converged rather than diverged -- each went one level deeper and the category is now enumerated and finite -- and because the rounds-exhausted rule exists to stop a search with no last element, which this no longer is. But the rule is the rule and this is the decision it asks for. WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE regardless of the answer: criterion 13 has held under three independent rounds of attack including five directions round 7 invented, and the code has been correct at every round -- what failed each time was the evidence that it was correct.
answer: READING 1. Decided by the user 2026-09-10. A projection is checked for whether it is applied CONSISTENTLY over its whole declaration; whether the value underneath is right belongs to the function that produces it, not to the projection of it. TASK-362 closes when every declared pair is compared from the KEY side: the ten subdict inner triples at bin/perry-state:2280-2289, the eleven arg-tuple names, and _at itself, which the tool and the test's expectation share. Bounded, finite, and round 7 specified the fix. THE FACT THAT DECIDES IT, measured rather than argued: --json is ALREADY pinned to the schema, just not in this module. tests/test_wip_and_stages.py:40 loads schema/state-schema.json, and round 7's MUT-2 (default_stages_for returns []) is GREEN on the compact module and RED on the full suite. So the chain holds by composition -- the schema pins --json, the projection walk pins --compact -- and the blind spot is in one module rather than in the coverage. THE RISK THIS READING ACCEPTS, stated so nobody discovers it later as a surprise: if build() reads the wrong source for a field, --json and --compact carry the SAME wrong number, the standup shows it, both payloads agree and every test passes. That is not criterion 5's subject under this reading, and it is real. It is filed as its own row rather than left implicit. WHY THIS IS NOT THE ROUNDS-EXHAUSTED RULE BEING WAIVED: that rule stops a search with no last element. Four rounds went one layer deeper each and the category is now counted -- ten triples, eleven names, one function. The code has been correct at every round; what failed each time was the evidence that it was correct.

title: perry-task add --track is accepted and dropped on a project-mode track
summary: MEASURED 2026-09-11 WHILE FIXING TASK-362, ON A WORKTREE OF 583f024f. bin/perry-task cmd_add writes values[track] only inside if mode != project, so a row filed with --track T against a PROJECT-mode track T is accepted, exits 0, and stores track main. Probed across all four modes: project stores main, pipeline/queue/inquiry store T. The consequence is not cosmetic and was found through it -- cmd_done reads track_of(config, values[track]), so the row closes at the IMPLICIT main track's Default rung instead of T's. Declaring T with Default rung V6 and closing a row raised with --track T stamps V3. THE COMMENT TWO LINES ABOVE THAT BRANCH REFUSES --stage FOR EXACTLY THIS REASON: 'Swallowing it is the same silent discard --commitment used to perform: the caller believes they set something.' --track is swallowed immediately below it. This is DESIGN-016 section 1.4's accepted-and-silently-dropped, the complaint that design was opened on, in the writer rather than the parser. The row must DECIDE which is right -- project mode may genuinely have one track, in which case --track on a project-mode track is a refusal and not a stored cell -- and then make the tests say so.

title: perry-diagnose reads the append-only journal as a live reference, so one mistyped id dirties a project forever
summary: MEASURED 2026-09-11 ON MAIN AT 7f43a11c. test_diagnose.TestUserLoadFindings.test_perry_itself_passes_its_own_id_checks went red on Perry's own project, reporting user_load.dangling == ['USER-920']. ISOLATED BY REMOVAL, one file at a time, on a scratch copy: with the journal's mention of USER-920 replaced the finding clears; with only the .perry/events.jsonl mention replaced it does not. THE JOURNAL LINE IS WHAT TRIPS IT. The board and the store each mention USER-920 once and have done since before 583f024f, where the same test passes -- so a live cell citing the id was never enough. What changed at 4a2cbea2 is that TASK-281's Next action was rewritten and the journal recorded the new text, which names USER-920. WHY THIS IS NOT A DATA FIX. The journal is append-only, so the reference cannot be withdrawn. And USER-920 can never be minted: mint_id only moves forward, so filing a row to satisfy the reference produced USER-926 on a probe, not USER-920. Neighbours USER-918, 919, 921 and 922 all have rows; 920 alone has none and never did -- git log -S for its board row finds no commit. The project is therefore permanently dirty by this check, through no act anyone can undo, which makes the test unusable as a gate and is the reason it is being reported rather than worked around. THE ROW MUST DECIDE what a reference is. A journal is history: an id cited in a record of what happened on a Tuesday is not a claim that the id exists now. If history stays in the domain, the check needs a remedy a project can perform. If it leaves, say what that costs -- the check exists to catch an id that is referenced and never defined, and a citation that appears ONLY in history is exactly the case where nobody will ever look again.

perry-goals computes KR progress from 157 of 430 task records, because it hands a project root where a state root is required
summary: FOUND BY TASK-348's CENSUS AND VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE PMO, 2026-09-11, ON MAIN. bin/perry-goals line 963 calls lib.task_status_index(getattr(snap, 'project_root', '.'), ...). The task store lives under the STATE root. Two lines above, the same function correctly passes snap.state_root to load_linkage_store with the comment 'state_root, not project_root: the store sits beside the register' -- so the right value is in hand and the wrong one is used. MEASURED ON PERRY'S OWN PROJECT, where the two roots differ (project root is the repository, state root is perry/): task_status_index called with project_root returns 157 rows, called with state_root returns 430, and the store holds 430 records. perry-goals therefore computes every KR's progress over 37 percent of the work, falling back to the 157 rendered board rows because the store is not where it looked. THE ANSWER IS PLAUSIBLE AND NOBODY CAN TELL: it returns a number, not an error, and no test compares it against perry-state's. This is review.md section 0's second question -- a tool reporting a wrong answer to someone with no way to detect it. It is invisible on a project whose two roots coincide, which is why it survived.

title: a row can close at verification V0, which the store accepts, perry-lint passes, and the writer refuses from a caller
summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 11 ON TASK-362 AND SHARPENED BY THE PMO'S INDEPENDENT CHECK, 2026-09-11. perry-config track --default-rung writes without validation and perry-task done stamps the cell verbatim. Measured on three values: Default rung 'banana' stores 'banana' and perry-lint reports 1 error; 'V9' stores 'V9' and lint reports 1 error; 'V0' stores 'V0' AND PERRY-LINT REPORTS 0 ERRORS. All three are refused at exit 1 when a caller passes the same value to done --rung. V0 is the one that matters and the reason is structural: V0 is IN schema enums.verification_rung, because a linter has to be able to name it, while check_rung refuses it by name as 'the label for what is being rejected, never a rung a row may carry'. So a closed row can carry V0 through the store, through the schema, and through the linter, and only the path a human types is guarded. THIS IS NOT CRITERION 13'S DEFECT and round 11 was right not to fail the row for it: the store holds what the payload publishes, so the equality criterion 13 asserts still holds. The defect is downstream and identical before and after round 10's fix. Round 11 filed it because it widens the bound rather than sitting inside it.

from: NO V4 HAS EVER RUN ON THIS ROW AND NONE CAN BE DISPATCHED TODAY -- read this before the V4 REVIEW label below, which is the author's intent and not an activity anyone is performing. MEASURED 2026-09-07: no evidence document carries a verdict block naming this row, and the row has NO WRITTEN CRITERIA -- there is no evidence/<month>/<id>-spec.md for it and its verification field is empty, so work/reference/review.md section 1 REFUSES the dispatch rather than let a fresh reviewer invent its own bar. The round the label names was killed by the 2026-09-04 rate limit and nothing re-dispatched it or noticed. THE CODE BELOW IS MERGED ON MAIN REGARDLESS, which is what makes this worth saying out loud: it is unverified merged code, not work in progress. TASK-379 carries both halves -- nothing reports a row parked at review without a verdict, and nothing could be sent if it did; TASK-278's V4 finally ran today and FAILED on data loss that had sat on main since its merge, which is the argument for not leaving these four as they are. THE AUTHOR'S ORIGINAL CELL FOLLOWS, UNCHANGED: V4 REVIEW. Merged, and I re-ran tests.test_host_support three times on the now-quiet machine: OK, OK, OK. THE HYPOTHESIS HELD AND THE MECHANISM IS EXACT: under load the losers exit 2, LOCK TIMEOUT, not 1, cap refusal -- THEY NEVER REACH THE CAP CHECK. Idle, all 17 losers are refused by the cap; under 16 burners, 17 to 19 are refused by the LOCK. So 'winners == 3' was never asserting the cap at all; it was asserting that all 20 contenders won the lock race inside LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT. THE TWO-WAY DECISION THE USER ASKED FOR, SETTLED WITH ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN PREFERENCE: one UNCONTENDED critical section costs 0.251s idle and 5.699s median / 11.833s max under load -- a 23x blow-up, because it shells out about ten times. Serialising 20 contenders therefore needs at least 114 SECONDS of lock budget against the 10 shipped, and the required budget SCALES WITH AMBIENT LOAD while a single critical section already exceeds the timeout. So NO FINITE RETRY BUDGET MAKES THE EXACT COUNT A PROMISE -- it only moves the load at which the test flips. Fix the assertion; do not add a retry. AND IT IS NOT A BARE <=: the new form is winners == min(cap, decided) over contenders that actually reached the cap check. Exact at any load, and it pins the decided-below-cap case too, so it cannot pass by everyone losing. A REAL PREVIOUSLY-UNREPRODUCED RACE IN bin/perry-dispatch-limit, section 5 of the result: a process that won mkdir has its lock directory removed underneath it before it writes owner, surfacing as 'mv: No such file or directory' and, through set -e, EXIT 1 -- INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A CAP REFUSAL. Six anomalies in eight rounds. THAT is what TASK-313's own title describes, so it is TASK-313's first concrete reproduction. IT ALSO CAUGHT ITSELF: its first attempt reintroduced the very bug it was fixing, by adding an assertion that counted those anomalous exit-1s as cap refusals; it went red immediately and is recorded in section 6. HONEST LIMIT, STATED NOT HIDDEN: under heavy load the contended test cannot detect an off-by-one cap. But the OLD assertion was red 6 of 6 at base under that load, so it detected nothing either -- and test_global_cap_still_wins is serial and stays red on that mutation under load. Serial tests own the arithmetic; contended tests own the race. MACHINE COST, section 10: about 45 to 60 minutes of oversubscription, burners tagged PERRYBURNER so they are countable rather than inferred, and all verified dead. It stopped the broad census after one run and traded it for a targeted measurement. Its stated constraint: this verification method is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE WITH PARALLEL DISPATCH -- and note the machine sat at load 109-121 from four OTHER agents with none of its burners running, so its 'idle' baseline was never truly idle.

title: DESIGN-022 A — KR checks and measurements are records, and met is derived on read
from: ASKED BY AIMARK 2026-09-09. CONFIRMED BY THE PMO AGAINST THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN AGREED: current_provenance.state is a TWO-VALUED vocabulary, asserted / unasserted, with measured as a separate boolean, and schema/goals-list-contract.md line 143 documents asserted_at empty as 'a real state and not an error: nobody wrote the date down'. So there is no third state available and the empty date is indeed the whole signal. THE CASE AIMARK BUILT IT ON: P003-O2-KR1 carries target 0, current 0, provenance asserted with measured false and asserted_at empty. Its metric prose says the number was measured by hand on 2026-09-07 and shows the grep that produced it, so the zero is real and hard-won -- and the payload's account of it is byte-identical to what a zero nobody ever touched looks like. THIS IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE DEFECT CONTRACT 2.1 ALREADY NAMED AND ONLY HALF-CLOSED. 2.1's note says the register template pre-fills current 0 so a drive-to-zero KR 'reads as achieved on the day it is written', and P002-O2-KR2 did exactly that; current_provenance and current_staleness shipped as the answer. They answer 'is this number stale' and they do not answer 'did anyone ever write this number'. The contract page even says an ABSENT current is null and unasserted, never 0 -- which is the right rule and is not what the template does. WHAT AIMARK DID ON ITS OWN SIDE, so this row does not re-litigate it: krProgress used to return null on any zero target to dodge a division; it now reads target 0 with current 0 as MET, because two numbers were stated and they agree, which is the same reading as target 3 current 3 and not a division at all. A zero target with a NON-zero current still returns null deliberately -- a count that went from four to one is three quarters done only if you know it started at four, and that baseline lives in metric prose. If Perry wants that bar drawn, the baseline has to become a field. DEPENDENCY ADDED 2026-09-10: waits on TASK-415, and this one IS logical as well as practical. TASK-415 establishes the principle in the contract page's own words -- a payload that publishes a measured number with nothing to place it against hands the consumer a value whose only honest rendering is nothing. THIS ROW IS THE SAME PRINCIPLE APPLIED TO THE ZERO CASE: a hand-measured zero and an untouched template row are byte-identical, so a consumer cannot tell a finished KR from one nobody ever wrote. Landing 415 first gives this row the vocabulary to be written in rather than inventing a second way to say the same thing on the same page. Both are minors on schema/goals-list-contract.md, so the changelog-renumbering argument applies here too.

title: A pipe-written tasks value is a hard lint error and, separately, resolves to nothing in a reader that never consults the linter
from: SEVERITY CORRECTED 2026-09-08, AND THE CORRECTION IS TO WHAT THE PMO WROTE ON THIS ROW. This row said a pipe-written tasks value declares an edge that is dropped SILENTLY, with no KR counting it, no attribution seeing it, and NO CHECK REPORTING IT MISSING. THE LAST CLAUSE IS FALSE. Found by TASK-278 round 3's V4 and reproduced by the PMO: planting `tasks: |` with the id on the following line draws a HARD LINT ERROR -- "perry/phase/002-linkage.md [bad-type] objectives[2].krs[1].tasks must be a list" -- so the register is refused outright rather than accepted with a lost edge. WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND IS WHY THE ROW SURVIVES: the READER still drops the edge. kr_for_task matches the id exactly and the block scalar yields the id plus a trailing newline, so the two halves disagree about the same input -- the linter calls the register malformed while the reader silently returns one fewer edge for it. A register in that state is refused by one tool and half-honoured by another, which is a smaller defect than a silent loss but is still two answers to one question. SO THE ROW IS NO LONGER ABOUT DATA LOSS. It is about a shape that fails a type check and, independently, resolves to nothing in a reader that never consults that check. Whoever takes it should decide whether the reader should refuse in the same terms the linter does, or whether being refused at lint time is sufficient and the reader's behaviour is unreachable in practice -- and MEASURE which, rather than assume, because the linter is not on every path that loads a register. DOWNGRADED FROM P1 TO P2 ON THAT BASIS. The original P1 rested on the silence, and the silence is not there.
to: Measure whether malformed pipe-written tasks can reach the reader without lint, then decide shared refusal versus sufficient lint rejection. Lint already gives a hard bad-type error; only the reader drops the edge. P2 correction stands; do not revive the silent-data-loss claim. See perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-447-next-action-accounts.md#task-386.

title: A mitigation that lives in one writer's body was not inherited by the next writer that read the same field
from: FOUND 2026-09-07 WHILE RECORDING TASK-155's REPRODUCTION, and it is that row's own prediction coming true one step worse. TASK-155's summary says its defect is disclosed at three layers and fixed at none, and warns that the cheapest wrong outcome is a FOURTH DISCLOSURE. What shipped instead is a fourth writer with NO disclosure. MEASURED, both sides on the same tree: bin/perry-goals:2226 builds a redated list of every KR whose assertion date the write is about to move, returns it as current_assertions_redated, and PRINTS a warning naming them -- with a comment stating why: naming it on every write is what keeps this from being discovered as a silent number months later, since the real fix is a new schema field behind the safety gate. bin/perry-tasks:1612, the linkage-write --from-register path built today by TASK-277, reads THE IDENTICAL field for declared_at, validates its FORMAT and refuses a day-only value -- and never reports what it re-dates. It rewrote declared_at on 115 records in one run with no warning at all. SO THE DEFECT WAS INHERITED AND THE DISCLOSURE WAS NOT. That is the failure mode this row is about: a mitigation that lives in one writer's body rather than in something every writer must pass through. A fifth writer will inherit the same way. WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is not just "add the warning to linkage-write": the disclosure exists because the fix is gated, so it is a standing obligation on every writer that reads updated: as a date. Either the obligation is enforced -- a shared helper that no writer can bypass, or a check that fails a writer reading that field without reporting -- or it is documentation and the next writer will skip it too. Note perry-goals' own comment says naming it is what buys time until the gated fix lands, so this row is about keeping that purchase, not about the fix itself.
to: Decide how every writer using updated: as assertion date must report re-dating (shared helper or enforceable check). linkage-write re-dated 115 records silently while perry-goals warned. The real schema fix remains gated; adding one local warning alone repeats the defect. See perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-447-next-action-accounts.md#task-387.

title: A design's Linked OKR line is parsed into a field nothing reads, so a design can name a KR that does not exist and every instrument stays green
from: FOUND AND MEASURED BY ADR-017's DOCUMENT ROUND, 2026-09-08, and it is the reason that half of the migration cannot land first. viewer/parsers.py:3397 parses the design header's Linked OKR line into a dataclass field, sets it at :3409, and NOTHING READS IT -- verified independently: no consumer anywhere in bin/, and not one reference in the whole of tests/. THE ROUND PROVED THE CONSEQUENCE RATHER THAN ARGUING IT: it renamed DESIGN-011's Linked OKR to a grammar nothing resolves and re-measured, and perry-lint stayed at 0 errors, the perry-diagnose finding set was byte-identical, no LOAD-02 appeared, and user_load.dangling -- the list test_diagnose asserts empty -- was [] BEFORE AND AFTER. So a design can point its Linked OKR at an id that does not exist and every instrument Perry has stays green. WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A DEAD FIELD: DESIGN documents declare which KR they serve in exactly this line, and that declaration is the thing a reader uses to answer "what goal is this design for". It is also adjacent to TASK-355 and TASK-282, which are about a locked design's implementation rows not citing it -- so the design-to-goal edge is unchecked in BOTH directions, and impl_refs is the only one of the two that any tool computes. THE DECISION IT FORCES IS ALREADY NAMED IN ADR-017 and is recorded as a Changes entry on that ADR: its Consequences say the seven locked design headers get a Changes entry rather than a header edit, "unless the lane decides the header field is METADATA rather than BODY". A field with no consumer is metadata by the plainest reading of that test, so the decide lane settled it that way and the header edits ride with the atomic data rename rather than becoming seven Changes entries in locked documents. WHAT THIS ROW IS FOR, and it is not the rename: either Linked OKR gets a consumer -- resolved against the OKR store, reported when it dangles, the way impl_refs is computed -- or it is deleted from the header template as decoration. Do not fix it by adding a lint rule alone: DESIGN-013's rule is that a fact with a schema lives in one store, and a design-to-KR edge is exactly that shape, which is what linkage.jsonl already does for task-to-KR.
to: Decide whether Linked OKR becomes a declared/resolved design-to-KR edge or leaves the template. Use ADR-017's mutation that left all checks green; a lint-only fix duplicates a schema fact. The lane already settled header metadata for the atomic rename; this row is not that rename. See perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-447-next-action-accounts.md#task-390.

title: A documented flag combination writes a linkage record that permanently reddens the suite, and the writer has no retraction
from: FOUND BY TASK-279's V4 AS ITS NEAREST MISS, FILED RATHER THAN FAILED, AND REPRODUCED BY THE PMO BEFORE MERGING. --actor is a DOCUMENTED flag, at perry-task add --help line 150. Run add --kr <KR> --actor goals in a scratch copy of main and the writer appends {"kind":"edge","task":...,"kr":...,"actor":"goals","via":"add"} and tests/test_linkage_import.py goes from 1 failure to 2, the new one being test_no_live_record_the_goals_lane_declared_was_stamped_via_add. THERE IS NO SUPPORTED REMEDY: the linkage writer is append-only and has no retraction, so the record cannot be withdrawn by any command Perry ships. A user following the help text can therefore redden the suite permanently in one invocation. ROOT CAUSE IS ONE ASYMMETRY: bin/perry-task:2797 takes the lane from the CALLER, while the importer hardcodes LINKAGE_IMPORT_ACTOR. So the same field is caller-supplied on one path and a constant on the other, and the test that TASK-279 round 2 scoped to actor == goals reads it as if only the importer could ever write it. WHY IT WAS NOT A FAIL, and the argument is defensible: the spec never mentions actor, DESIGN-015 section 7 records that NOTHING ENFORCES THE LANE TABLE YET, the record itself is TRUE -- the goals lane really did declare it -- and it is counted correctly by the KR. The module is also already permanently red on any add --kr under TASK-383, so this adds a second failure to a module that is red either way. AND THE JUSTIFICATION FOR THE SCOPE IT EXPLOITS IS FACTUALLY WRONG. Round 2 scoped the assertion to actor == goals on the reasoning that such a record would be "a genuine lane lie". The V4 measured --actor agent against --actor goals and THE KR COUNTER SCORES THEM IDENTICALLY AT 100 PERCENT, with no disagreement anywhere. So the scope is pinned by mutation but its stated reason does not hold, which is why this row exists rather than a note on TASK-279. WHAT TO DECIDE: either the lane on a linkage record is not caller-supplied -- the writer stamps the lane it IS, the way the importer does -- or the assertion stops keying on a field a caller controls. Do not fix it by refusing --actor with --kr alone; that leaves the same field caller-supplied everywhere else it is stamped.
to: Decide writer-owned lane stamping versus an assertion that does not trust caller-controlled actor. TASK-279 V4 reproduced --kr with --actor goals; counters agree but tests redden and no retraction exists. Do not merely forbid that flag combination; reconcile TASK-383's existing red. See perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-447-next-action-accounts.md#task-391.

title: TASK-474 has FAILed V4 twice and both FAILs are one undecided principle: WHO OWNS NEWLINE NORMALISATION for a tier-1 phase document. Round 1: perry-goals split lines two ways internally. Round 2: the splitter was unified but the READER was not — perry-goals reads a body with read_bytes().decode() (byte-faithful, a lone CR is not a line break) while perry-lint reads with read_text() (universal newlines, a lone CR IS one). A 300-line body containing one CR is written at exit 0 and the project's own linter immediately calls it 301 lines over a hard cap of 300. Reproduced by me, not taken on the reviewer's report. Rule 1 says enumerate the category; two FAILs means the category is a fork nobody has taken, so this is the choice rather than a third round. (A) THE WRITER NORMALISES: phase new translates every line break in the supplied body to LF before writing, so the bytes on disk contain only LF and every reader agrees whatever call it uses. Defensible applied consistently: one owner, one place, and the cap count stops depending on who asks. Cost: the writer silently rewrites the author's bytes, which is exactly what Okr.render refuses to do and says so in its docstring — a document that still lints and no longer reads the way its author wrote it. (B) ONE DECLARED READ RULE ACROSS TOOLS: perry-goals and perry-lint are made to read identically, guarded across bin/ rather than inside one function pair. Defensible applied consistently: nothing rewrites anyone's bytes, and the rule becomes checkable for every current and future reader. Cost: it touches bin/perry-lint and any other reader, which is outside TASK-474's declared Files in scope, so it widens this row or becomes its own. WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE: the phase lifecycle writer is merged on main at 8b6078f7; both suites were green; the round-2 review PASSes criteria 1, 2, 6, 7, 8 and 9 and FAILs 3, with 5 flagged. perry-goals already carries the rule for the SPLIT half in two docstrings and a guard added this round. Nothing in schema/state-schema.json declares how a line is counted; bin/perry-lint decides it at :844. I RECOMMEND (A) for the cap path only, not for the document body: count the cap from a normalised copy so the gate agrees with the linter, and keep writing the author's bytes unchanged. That takes neither cost — no rewrite of the user's text, no edit to another tool — and it is the narrowest thing that makes criterion 3 true. Say A, B, my narrowed A, or stop the row.
